    • I will keep this to the same three areas: join elimination, result downloads and Iceberg.
    • Note: The current capabilities below are from public documentation checked on November 13, 2026, not a fresh benchmark.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that I had shared a post on LinkedIn comparing a few Snowflake and Databricks capabilities with what was available around mid-2023. Our earlier warehouse POC covered Athena, Dremio, Redshift and Snowflake. Going through the documentation again, there are a few things I would revisit before using those findings for another decision.

    I will keep this to the same three areas: join elimination, result downloads and Iceberg.

    Note: The current capabilities below are from public documentation checked on November 13, 2026, not a fresh benchmark. The earlier POC observations apply to the configurations we tested then; we have not tested the newer capabilities and integrations described here.

    Industry observers note that let us take a sales report which only needs total revenue. The BI tool may still generate a join between the sales and customer tables because that relationship exists in its model.

    Recent findings suggest that if the query doesn't use any customer attributes, the database may be able to skip that join. It needs valid key relationships to establish that doing so won't change the result. Duplicate customer keys, for example, could multiply the sales rows.

    It has been revealed that snowflake had documented join-elimination improvements by July 2022. Its RELY constraints let the optimizer use declared relationships for qualifying optimizations. Snowflake documentation, 2022 release history.

    Sources indicate that for the Databricks pattern I discussed, I couldn't find documented support at the mid-2023 point. Primary-key RELY is now documented from Runtime 14.2, released in November 2023. Foreign-key RELY followed in Runtime 15.4 and the September 2024 SQL release. Requirements, Runtime 14.2, SQL release history.

    Recent findings suggest that so this is something I would no longer keep as a Snowflake-only advantage. Redshift also documents using primary and foreign keys to remove redundant joins. I haven't established when that was introduced. Redshift documentation.

    The supported Databricks compute and table types need checking; classic SQL warehouses are excluded. Also, declaring a key doesn't make the data valid. Incorrect key declarations can lead to incorrect results.

    For a large BI extract, query execution may finish while the client is still downloading rows. We looked at this during the earlier evaluation because the compute behavior during that download can affect cost.

    Sources indicate that snowflake persists completed results separately from the warehouse cache. Its result-storage and suspension behavior allow later retrieval without keeping warehouse compute active solely for that retrieval. Auto-suspend settings and other running work still matter. Persisted results, warehouse suspension.

    In a recent development, databricks has Cloud Fetch to download larger results directly from cloud storage. This was available before mid-2023. Its current monitoring documentation also claims SQL warehouses remain active while queries are running or fetching results. Cloud Fetch, warehouse monitoring.

    It has been revealed that when we tested Redshift during the earlier evaluation, we had to keep the compute running until the client finished downloading the results. We were therefore paying for the full extract duration, not just query execution.

    According to recent reports, we have not repeated that test on current Redshift or Databricks configurations. The earlier Redshift finding applies to the setup we tested; today’s behavior and cost need checking with the warehouse, connector and workload we intend to use.

    Sources indicate that iceberg was one of the formats we were following in 2023. Snowflake Iceberg Tables became generally available in June 2024. Since then, the available integration options have expanded. Snowflake release.

    The important detail is where the table's catalog is managed:.

    Snowflake-managed access, external-catalog writes, Databricks Iceberg, Redshift Iceberg SQL.

    Multiple engines do not necessarily need to write to the same table. The distinction matters when a team wants to keep its existing catalog and use another engine for transformations. Databricks’ native foreign Iceberg integration is documented as read-only; external engines can read and write Unity Catalog-managed Iceberg through its REST API. Whether that restriction matters depends on the intended architecture.

    According to recent reports, redshift has changed considerably here. Iceberg querying became generally available in November 2023, append-only writes in November 2025, and REVISION, DELETE and MERGE in April 2026. That old “not supported” entry needs another look. Querying, inserts, row-level changes.

    It has been revealed that snowflake also added on-demand table registration for catalog-linked databases on November 3, 2026. A remote table can be registered when referenced, without waiting for the next catalog sync. Release note.

    Dremio was part of the original POC. SAP completed its acquisition on July 6, 2026, and has described how Dremio technology fits into SAP Business Data Cloud's Iceberg and open-catalog direction. For teams combining SAP and non-SAP data, I would include that in another evaluation. Acquisition, SAP upgrade.

    Sources indicate that microsoft Fabric could be considered as well, particularly by teams already using Power BI. It wasn't in the original POC. Its Warehouse and Lakehouse experiences around OneLake give us another option to evaluate. Microsoft overview.

    With AI in the mix, I feel product teams are shipping features faster than ever. As an architect, I still need to look further ahead: how the firm works, the people who will maintain the platform, business direction, contracts and the overall financial commitment.

    Sources indicate that I wouldn't change platforms just because a feature was released. But I also wouldn't use a limitation from an old POC to rule one out without checking it again.

    If you have recently tested these result-download or Iceberg scenarios on Databricks or Redshift, please share your experience. I would be interested to know what you observed.

    AI anxiety: 5 ways to cope when you’re scared of AI

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that if you’re feeling a mix of emotions about artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and how they’re shaping our world, you’re not alone.
    • Industry observers note that AI anxiety is the worry or unease some people feel about the fast growth of artificial intelligence and how quickly technology is changing.
    • According to recent reports, AI research goes back decades, but progress has sped up sharply in recent years with the arrival of chatbots, AI image generators, and other tools.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you’re feeling a mix of emotions about artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and how they’re shaping our world, you’re not alone. Chief Clinical Officer at Calm, Chris Mosunic, PhD, has tips and strategies to help tame a growing source of anxiety.

    Industry observers note that AI anxiety is the worry or unease some people feel about the fast growth of artificial intelligence and how quickly technology is changing. It isn’t a clinical diagnosis, but the feelings are real and common. They can focus on everyday risks, such as job loss and AI-powered scams, and bigger ones, such as AI getting out of human control.

    According to recent reports, AI research goes back decades, but progress has sped up sharply in recent years with the arrival of chatbots, AI image generators, and other tools. A 2023 Calm survey* found that nearly 1 in 3 U.S. adults (29%) felt anxious about AI, and 18% described their feelings as fear or dread. At the same time, 31% felt optimistic, and 31% felt excited. Many respondents felt a mix: amazed by AI and nervous about it.

    In a recent development, concern about AI has stayed high in the years since. In a June 2026 Pew Research Center survey, 52% of U.S. adults noted they feel more concerned than excited about AI in daily life. That’s up from 37% in 2021 and about the same as in 2023. Just 9% said they feel more excited than concerned.

    It has been revealed that it’s hard to know how AI will affect our safety and our lives. You might wonder how it will change your job, what it could mean for areas like scientific research, and what the future will look like. Many of us find uncertainty hard to cope with, so feeling anxious or out of control is understandable. But when anxiety feels overwhelming, it can start to affect your sleep, mood, and focus.

    These five ways to manage AI anxiety draw on mindfulness and common thinking traps, like catastrophizing. Start with whichever fits how you feel today.

    The rapid rise in AI and automation can feel like a threat to our livelihoods (and even our lives), making many of us feel unstable and out of control.

    In a recent development, resist resisting: When confronted with uncertainty, our first instinct can often be to fight it. Try sitting with it instead. Notice how the discomfort shows up in your body and mind.

    Go at your own pace: Give yourself time to adjust to the fresh realities of AI.

    Talk it out: Process your anxieties with a friend or a coworker. You may find someone who feels the same way.

    💙 On those days when you feel overwhelmed by the rapidly changing tech landscape, try a simple meditation practice like Pause to Breathe to help you feel more grounded.

    If you’re feeling anxious or uneasy about AI, don’t invalidate or try to avoid those emotions — that approach can make things worse. Instead, let yourself feel anxious. Telling yourself you’re overreacting can damage your self-trust and self-confidence.

    According to recent reports, identify the emotions: Get a better understanding of what you’re feeling. Your anxiety could mean you’re working through a more deeply rooted problem, like feeling threatened or inadequate.

    Try meditation: Meditation can help you ground yourself in the present moment and tune into what you’re feeling and where it’s coming from.

    Write down all your anxieties without censoring yourself: Set aside dedicated time each day to think through your anxious thoughts, helping you process and make sense of your emotions.

    💙 Take some time to stop and do this short Emotions Check-In to make space for any anxious feelings.

    Industry observers note that when we’re feeling anxious about the unknown, many of us fall into the trap of catastrophic thinking, imagining the worst possible outcome, even without evidence to support it. This can cause low-level anxieties to spiral out of control.

    Challenge your worst fears: What evidence do you have that they’re true or that they’ll happen?

    In a recent development, bring to mind times in the past that felt groundbreaking in the tech world: Think back to the creation of mobile phones, laptops, or even navigation apps, and consider how you’ve adapted to their existence despite any initial anxieties or concerns. The same could happen with AI.

    Bring your mind back to the now: The future feels a whole lot less intimidating when you focus on the present.

    💙 One of the best ways you can bring yourself back to the present is through mindfulness meditation, which you can learn in the Mindfulness for Beginners series.

    Many of us find ourselves viewing situations as an all-or-nothing approach. This is a cognitive distortion called polarized thinking, and it often occurs because we’re focused on the extremes without considering the nuances or possibilities of any given situation.

    The debate around AI is nuanced. Popular culture shows dystopian futures, so it can be easy to think there’s only one possible outcome with AI.

    In a recent development, however, reality tends to exist in between the extremes, so remind yourself that it’s perfectly normal for opposing emotions or views to be present at the same time. And they can also all feel as strong, real, or true as each other. You can feel fascinated and terrified, anxious and excited, or resentful and grateful.

    When we allow multiple truths to co-exist in our minds, we make space for more ease. So try to hold space for the contradictions and the possibilities.

    💙 For a more in-depth discussion on how to use mindfulness to combat worrying and keep nuance at the forefront, check out the Overcome Stress & Anxiety series.

    In a recent development, at the extreme end of AI anxiety, some of us may have a deep—even subconscious—fear about a machine taking over. We ask questions like: Is this the beginning of the end of humanity? Will humans be replaced by robots?

    Sources indicate that A fear of overdependence on technology can cause us to worry about the negative consequences of relying too heavily on artificial intelligence. One way to remedy this fear is to embrace our humanity.

    Be present for the little things you often take for granted, like hugs, laughing until it hurts, or exchanging a look with your best friend.

    Make time for the people in your life, and prioritize connecting with them face-to-face when you can.

    Marvel at the awesomeness of human things like awkward silences or goosebumps when you’re listening to music.

    Ask people how they’re really feeling and practice deep listening when they respond.

    Disconnect from technology and spend time in nature.

    💙 Embrace the power of being human and living in the now by reading a book, listening to a meditation, or taking a Mindful Walk.

    *Calm research was fielded among n = 450 adults in the US between March 21, 2023 and March 22, 2023 and is nationally representative, with quotas across age, gender, race, ethnicity, and region.

    In a recent development, recent news stories have shown how general-purpose AI tools may respond in unsafe or harmful ways, especially when people are vulnerable or struggling with a mental health crisis. These situations are rare, but they highlight an important truth: AI is not human and can’t accurately recognize risk, provide crisis support, or understand the complexity of your emotional world.

    Sources indicate that AI can support mental health — especially when it’s part of a program designed and guided by licensed professionals. But general AI tools, like chatbots or large language models, are not a replacement for real human care.

    If you’re struggling, please consider reaching out to a therapist or support line — many offer free or low-cost options. You deserve support that’s personal, thoughtful, and real.

    In a recent development, U.S. - Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

    Worldwide - Visit findahelpline.com for free, confidential resources.

    Your mental health matters and you don’t have to navigate tough moments alone.

    To manage anxiety about artificial intelligence, there are proactive steps you can take.

    Educate yourself about AI to understand its capabilities and limitations better: Learning about AI can make it feel less intimidating.

    Engage in conversations about AI: Talking with others about your concerns can offer upcoming perspectives and reduce feelings of isolation.

    Practice mindfulness and stress-reduction techniques: Managing your anxiety effectively can help you focus on the present and reduce worries about the future.

    Stay informed about AI developments: Understand how it's being integrated into society to help you feel more prepared and less anxious.

    According to recent reports, fear of artificial intelligence is common and can stem from several concerns, such as uncertainty about how AI will affect the future, including potential changes in the job market and societal norms. You may also have concerns about privacy, security, and the ethical use of AI. The idea of losing control to machines or facing decisions made by algorithms without empathy can be daunting.

    Understanding these fears and addressing them through education and dialogue can help alleviate the anxiety associated with AI.

    Sources indicate that you don’t have to be, though some concern is understandable. AI is changing fast, and it raises real questions, from job loss and scams to whether people can keep control of it. Some risks deserve attention. Others are far from certain, and no one knows exactly how AI will unfold. When we’re anxious, our minds jump to the worst outcome and can treat every headline as proof of a disastrous future.

    Industry observers note that it can help to follow reliable news sources and take breaks from stories that leave you on edge. When your thoughts race ahead, try a mindfulness practice to bring your attention back to today. If worry about AI is getting in the way of sleep or daily life, consider talking with a therapist or doctor.

    The fear of AI doesn’t have a widely recognized specific term but is often considered a form of “technophobia,” which is the fear of advanced technology or complex devices. When this fear centers on AI, it can stem from concerns that the technology could surpass human intelligence and from the ethical consequences of machines making decisions that affect people’s lives. AI anxiety is rooted in the unknown future impact of AI on humanity.

    While AI offers many benefits, concerns about its negative effects remain. These include potential job losses due to automation, as AI can perform some tasks more efficiently than humans. Privacy issues are also a significant concern, as AI systems can process vast amounts of personal data, sometimes without clear consent or transparency. Security risks may arise if AI systems are hacked or malfunction. AI can also perpetuate bias if its training data is biased, leading to unfair or unethical decisions.

    On a societal level, increased reliance on AI could reduce human interaction and erode certain skills as machines take over more tasks. Understanding these potential negative effects can help develop strategies to mitigate them and ensure AI is used responsibly and ethically.

    #22897. Breaking: This Chain Was Dunkin's Bitter Rival In The '50s — Now It's The Most Popular Donut Spot In Japan

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (606 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: This Chain Was Dunkin's Bitter Rival In The '50s — Now It's The Most Popular Donut Spot In Japan

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that dunkin' is one of America's favorite spots to grab a quick donut and one of its famous syrup-infused iced coffees — which we ranked from worst to best.
    • It has been revealed that what makes this feud particularly fascinating is that it was a family affair.
    • Industry observers note that as is often the case, feuds rarely end with a clear winner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that dunkin' is one of America's favorite spots to grab a quick donut and one of its famous syrup-infused iced coffees — which we ranked from worst to best. Today, the chain boasts more than 10,000 stores in the U.S. alone and sits comfortably at the top of the country's donut hierarchy. However, it wasn't always the undisputed heavyweight. In a rivalry that gives McDonald's and Burger King a run for their money, Dunkin' spent decades going head-to-head with Mister Donut. Ultimately, Dunkin' came out on top — at least, if we're talking strictly about the USA. Over in Japan, Mister Donut reigns supreme.

    It has been revealed that what makes this feud particularly fascinating is that it was a family affair. Dunkin', originally known as Dunkin' Donuts, was founded in 1950 by William Rosenberg. The simple combination of donuts and coffee proved to be a huge success. Naturally, Rosenberg wanted to expand the business through franchising. So far, so good, right? Well, not everyone was happy with the idea, including Harry Winokur, Rosenberg's brother-in-law. In a move that would spark a decades-long rivalry, Winokur left the business and opened Mister Donut just a few miles from Dunkin's original location. He even embraced franchising, with Mister Donut employees reportedly being prohibited from saying the word "dunk" in their stores.

    Industry observers note that as is often the case, feuds rarely end with a clear winner. In 1990, Dunkin' acquired Mister Donut and rebranded nearly all of its American locations as Dunkin' stores (ouch). Today, just one Mister Donut location remains in the U.S. That must have been a hit on Winokur's pride, but while Dunkin' was busy making cereal in the '80s, Mister Donut was thriving on the other side of the world. Today, Mister Donut is Japan's leading donut chain, with more than 900 locations in operation.

    Sources indicate that japan has embraced plenty of Western-style foods with open arms. Think of the juicy, hamburger-inspired hambāgu, or comforting pizza toast with its wide array of toppings. Mister Donut also happens to fit comfortably into this category. However, one thing worth knowing about Japan's take on Western staples is that they're rarely direct copies. Instead, the country has a knack for putting its own spin on imported dishes. That's exactly how Mister Donut managed to carve out a place for itself in the market.

    The first Mister Donut opened its doors in Japan in 1971, after business executive Seiichi Suzuki acquired the exclusive rights to operate the brand in the country. The original menu featured familiar American favorites, but Suzuki also introduced items and adjustments designed to appeal to local tastes. These included reducing the sugar content of certain products, serving more modest portions, and creating a cozy, sit-down atmosphere. The approach proved successful, and Mister Donut quickly expanded across Japan. Dunkin', meanwhile, had also tried its luck in the Japanese market, opening its first location in 1970. While Mister Donut continued to grow, Dunkin' struggled to gain a foothold and eventually left Japan altogether in 1998.

    In 1989, Suzuki's manufacturer Duskin acquired full ownership of Mister Donut's Japanese operations, giving it greater freedom to develop the brand's distinctly Japanese identity. From there, the chain continued to expand, eventually bringing its donuts to markets including Thailand, Australia, Taiwan, and Singapore. Today, Mister Donut is best known for its playful, distinctly Japanese creations, particularly the Pon De Ring, a chewy, ring-shaped donut made up of small dough balls, and Mocchurin, its mochi-inspired donut line that is so soft, they require paper trays to keep each donut from losing its shape.

    Skip Tortilla Chips: Make Totchos For 10x The Flavor & Texture

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The appeal of nachos is easy to understand: Cover tortilla chips with a variable mix of cheese, meat, and beans, and dig into a mouth-watering textural experience.
    • It has been revealed that at first glance, it may seem like potatoes and nacho toppings shouldn't go together; tots are often a breakfast dish, after all.
    • So layer on ingredients like gooey cheese, corn and beans, flavorful ground meat or chorizo, salsa, pickled jalapeños, and more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The appeal of nachos is easy to understand: Cover tortilla chips with a variable mix of cheese, meat, and beans, and dig into a mouth-watering textural experience. It's a dish concept that originated in Mexico, but it has since become widely popularized in the USA, welcoming many modifications in the process. Want a version with a thick boost in flavor and texture? Make a batch of totchos, swapping the tortilla chips for miniature hash browns (aka tater tots).

    It has been revealed that at first glance, it may seem like potatoes and nacho toppings shouldn't go together; tots are often a breakfast dish, after all. Yet the spuds make for an excellent starchy flavor canvas, ready for whatever nacho fixings you throw on. Like other loaded tater tot recipes, it's all about contrasting flavors atop a canvas of crispy potatoes.

    So layer on ingredients like gooey cheese, corn and beans, flavorful ground meat or chorizo, salsa, pickled jalapeños, and more. Some bites will get a little wet, but most will remain crunchy. Yet since tater tots are much thicker than chips, the underside retains a sturdy foundation, propping up a nacho twist with a little more heft. It's among the most delicious hacks for a bag of frozen tater tots, meshing together a freezer classic item with a crowd favorite formula.

    According to recent reports, A platter of totchos fits a variety of contexts. Layer on an abundance of festive components, and the dish can be an all-out party platter. Keep it to a simple meat and cheese, and you get an affordable and comforting rendition. Whichever route you go for, construct the dish with a few considerations in mind to optimize both flavor and texture.

    When preparing the tater tots, aim for peak crunch, so cook them well before you add your toppings. A hot oven gets the job done, but consider also using the air fryer for restaurant-level crunch, or even pan-frying the tots — maybe even in chorizo fat for added flavor. Next in importance is how to incorporate the dairy, another nacho cornerstone.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're making a liquidy nacho cheese sauce, you can simply drizzle the condiment onto your tots. However, if you're using shredded cheese, you'll want to melt the component on top of the tots in the oven for around five minutes. During this step, you can include already prepped ground beef taco meat, too, melding the dish components alongside the bed of potatoes.

    Industry observers note that only right before serving should you include cold ingredients. Keep it simple with chopped lettuce and onions, a light drizzle of sour cream or crema, or consider something more complex, like pico de gallo and guacamole. Cilantro and scallions are always welcome, as is a squeeze of lime. Dig in with a fork and knife (and we do suggest using cutlery — unlike with chips, you won't be easily able to grab individual tots); totchos's hearty appeal is immediate — it's the magic of nachos, with a heftier base.

    It has been revealed that there's hardly a saying that expresses unbridled joy like "kid in a candy store." But why do kids get all the fun? Candy stores, those brightly colored meccas of sky-high sugar intake, beckon many Americans far into adulthood. Candy, after all, is one of those food products that can really take us back, so candy stores are capable of injecting a sense of nostalgia, childlike reverie, and excitement into anyone's day.

    Candy has long been a staple of American culture, with the oldest candy stores in the United States stretching back into past centuries. In the modern world, however, candy enthusiasts keep tabs on their favorite indulgences through candy-focused blogs, sweets-obsessed Instagram accounts, and TikTok viral candy sensations. Meanwhile, towns, states, and even nationwide publications regularly hold contests for the best candy store in the area (or in the country). These sources, and more, inspired this list of the coolest candy stores in the United States.

    Sources indicate that and in a society where more is more, candy stores have evolved from quaint little shops (still worth a visit for transporting yourself to the past) to mega-sized outlets overflowing with sweets. Some have blossomed into department store-level or warehouse-like square footage, others have added attractions far beyond the candy itself, from mini golf to candy museums, and some are just old-time-tastic. The candy stores listed here are not just the perfect places to get your candy fix. They've become must-visit destinations for travelers around the country.

    According to recent reports, philadelphia's Shane Confectionery is one of America's oldest candy stores — in fact, it's the oldest continuously operated confectionery. The company emphasizes that this claim to fame means that its operation has been consistently making and selling confections longer than any other site in America, in a historic four-story brick building that's survived for over 150 years.

    Industry observers note that but it wasn't until 1910, when the tech giant was sold to Edward R. Shane, that many of the retail shop's intricate, old-fashioned design elements were put into place. As the company explains, Shane installed elaborately carved cabinets, curved glass showcases, and marble countertops to highlight his confections, as well as stained glass transom windows above the storefront to allure passersby in front of his shop. Best of all, many of these architectural details have been restored and are on display in the shop today, making a visit there a bit like stepping into a charming bygone era.

    It's no wonder that Eater Philadelphia has called Shane Confectionery the "time portal to Philadelphia's sugary past," calling out the efforts of current owners, brothers Ryan and Eric Berley, who breathed new life into the longstanding business in 2011. Fans regularly show it love online as a must-visit when living in or traveling through the City of Brotherly Love.

    110 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19106.

    Industry observers note that with enthusiastic reviews and a high rankings online, Sweet Pete's Candy in Jacksonville, Florida, is hailed as the largest candy store in the Southeast. And the setting can't be beat: Visit Jacksonville points out that it's located in a historic 22,000-square-foot mansion right in the heart of downtown. From sour candies to hand-pulled lollipops, Sweet Pete's has your candy cravings covered.

    Sweet Pete's Candy also gets a leg up on the candy competition by serving customers with dietary restrictions. It offers an entire allergy-friendly array of candies, including a selection of gluten-free, dairy-free, vegan-friendly, and nut-free options. A classic treat is Pete's Famous Sea Salt Caramel, now available in different flavors, like Apple Pie.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, visitors can make a day out of their visit, because Sweet Pete's also houses Fizzies & Fare, an in-house restaurant and bar that's touted by the manufacturer as home to hundreds of unique craft sodas, over-the-top Crazy Shakes, classic American eats, candy-inspired cocktails, and more. Candy fans can also learn how their favorite candies are made through a guided tour, led by one of the staff's "Candy Connoisseurs," through the three-story "candy mansion," then grab their own handmade custom chocolate bar fresh from Sweet Pete's kitchen. The business even hosts parties, events, field trips for local school kids, and classes on-site.

    400 N Hogan St, Jacksonville, FL 32202.

    Sweet Mickey's, in the Ballard neighborhood of Seattle, is named after owner Randy Brinker's grandma and pays homage to her bygone party shop and homemade sweets. Many publications laud it as one of the best candy stores in the country, thanks to its variety of homemade fudges and truffles alongside classic candy favorites like Sugar Babies and international sensations like Danish salted licorice.

    Industry observers note that with a storefront tucked into the charming brick buildings of historic Ballard, it's the perfect place for a candy store with a vintage vibe and an old-time Americana aesthetic. From handmade goodies to its carefully curated selection of traditional and artisanal sweets from around the globe, candy lovers (or even the pickiest of eaters) can find something for them.

    Even better, this candy store has a heart. Since its 2012 grand opening, it has supported the local Little League, sponsored movie nights in the park, and hosted onsite parties and events to create sweet memories and build community.

    5338 Ballard Ave NW, Seattle, WA 98107.

    Recent findings suggest that it'Sugar, with candy-colored locations nationwide, was already known for its San Francisco flagship location, with a three-floor candy store in Fisherman's Wharf. The brand, with locations from coast to coast, then opened a 24,000-square-foot location in East Rutherford, New Jersey's American Dream shopping mall. This location, dubbed the World's First Candy Department Store, also spans three floors, though there are plenty across the country.

    Some of its over-the-top features at the East Rutherford location include: a three-story-tall Statue of Liberty replica covered in more than 1.5 million Jelly Belly beans, an immersive lollipop garden filled with nearly 10,000 lollipops, dozens of branded shops like Sour Patch Kids, Swedish Fish, Nerds, Starburst, and Reese's. It's truly a candy lover's dream come true. YouTubers have hailed it as an amazing feat of candy awesomeness, all a stone's throw from Fresh York City.

    The brand It'Sugar calls itself a "retailtainer," a mashup of retailer and entertainment. As company lore explains, the brand was founded by candy veteran Jeff Rubin in 2006 and has grown to more than 120 locations throughout the United States and Canada. It's known for "absurd sugar innovations" and the Sugar High Club, with which loyal visitors can earn points for their purchases — then, of course, they can cash them in for more sugar.

    It has been revealed that cleveland hosts North America's largest candy store, going strong for more than 75 years: b.a. Sweetie Candy Company. Cleveland.com calls it Cleveland's version of Willy Wonka's Candy Factory, and for good reason. Company stats boast that it hosts more than 500,000 visitors per year (making it one of the city's top attractions) and stocks more than 5,500 items in its wholesale store, to the tune of over $5 million in inventory on-hand at any given time.

    It has been revealed that with classic candy, retro candy, bulk candy, wholesale candy, and more, the store promises "the absolute largest variety of candy available anywhere in North America." Meaning, if you need 1,000 pounds of Tootsie Rolls to throw a parade, it's your outlet. It even keeps an eye on bygone favorites and claims it has been instrumental in bringing back vintage candies that had disappeared from shelves, including nostalgic names like Bonomo's Turkish Taffy, Slo Poke, Regal Crown, and Broadway licorice rolls.

    Industry observers note that all that would be enough to lure any candy fan, but b.a. Sweetie Candy Tech giant is much more than just a candy store. It's a bona fide family-fun destination, offering Golfland Park, which has two 18-hole mini golf courses, complete with lights for evening play, koi ponds, a cascading waterfall, and concession stands. Meanwhile, the Soda Shoppe serves up homemade ice cream, sundaes, malts, and over 100 sodas in a barn-style parlor.

    6770 Brookpark Rd, Cleveland, OH 44129.

    It has been revealed that this Latest York City treasure actually started as a shoe and hat repair shop — but a little push cart outside also sold candy. According to company lore, in the Depression years, 1937, the business owners decided to focus on their biggest moneymaker, candy, and became known as Economy Candy. After World War II, Morris "Moishe" Cohen and his brother in law assumed ownership and expanded the business, selling candy, chocolate, gift baskets, dried fruit, nuts, and more. Morris' son, Jerry, and his wife, Ilene, took over after its move to the current location at 108 Rivington Street, then passed the business to son Mitchell, who runs it today.

    In other words, this living legend is a true family affair — and a multigenerational sensation that has become a part of the rich history of Newly introduced York City. In 2023, the northwest corner of Rivington and Essex Streets were co-named Morris "Moishe" Cohen Way in honor of Morris and Economy Candy's lasting legacies.

    Today, the store still boasts over 2,000 items for sale, and visitors routinely rave about its massive selection and reasonable prices online. Hot sellers include chocolate-covered graham crackers (with and without jelly), chocolate-covered pretzels, jelly rings, gummies, and those hard-to-find candy bars. For those outside New York City, Economy Candy offers online sales, as well.

    108 Rivington St, Newly introduced York, NY 10002.

    Industry observers note that A candy shop with old-fashioned soda fountain treats like ice cream, specialty chocolate candies and fudge, more than 400 candies for buying in bulk, and 3,000-plus wrapped candies — all in colorful circus-theme surroundings? Yes, please.

    It has been revealed that the Substantial Top Candy Shop has been serving the Austin community (as well as candy-minded travelers) since 2007. Visitors praised its wall-to-wall candy selection, laid out in candy-colored rows, jars, racks, and even in a lollipop tree. Passing by Peanuts, the elephant pictured on the shop's entrance (facing the city's famed South Congress Avenue, known for housing quirky boutiques), visitors will find a whimsical wonderland at Big Top Candy with classic soda machines, retro candies, and a hefty bulk section customers can grab by the scoop.

    Industry observers note that the store promises both nostalgic favorites and new creations from around the globe. Whether you're just passing through for SXSW or a stalwart resident, Substantial Top Candy Shop is a must-visit in the Live Music Capital of the World.

    1706 S Congress Ave, Austin, TX 78704.

    Minnesota's Largest Candy Store in Jordan, Minnesota, nods to its mind-boggling mass of inventory in its very name — and the company would seem intent on living up to that moniker. Owned by Robert Wagner, and also known as Jim's Apple Farm, the store houses not only nostalgic candy, but fresh-baked pies and strudels, the world's largest selection of sodas, an array of popcorn flavors, and locally-sourced items (think pastas, jams, jellies, and even puzzles). These are all sourced from surrounding farms, making this Midwestern gem not only a candy emporium but a true shopping destination that supports locals and promotes Minnesota products to everyone who enters.

    Recent findings suggest that fortunately, its location is relatively convenient for passers-through, as the store is only 35 miles from Minneapolis. And you can't miss it — the store is housed in a massive, bright yellow barn. It's a must-stop not only thanks to its dizzying array of sweet and savory treats, but fun touches throughout its interior decor, such as a fresh observatory-like dome featuring a mural with more than two dozen superheroes, an animatronic band, and a fortune-telling machine.     Sources indicate that with 135 years of history, Schimpff's Confectionery more than deserves those honors — its recipes and business stretch back to the 1800s. And it's still making waves, having been featured on several reveals and publications.

    In a recent development, with such an illustrious history, it makes sense that Schimpff's Confectionery also houses a candy museum, with thousands of pieces of American candy memorabilia. Customers will find not just a store, but an unforgettable experience at The Peppermint Stick Candy Store & Ice Cream Parlor.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that when it comes to the Thanksgiving feast, Americans' favorite sides include mashed potatoes, green bean casserole, and of course, stuffing. Whether it comes from a box or is lovingly homemade, stuffing is a filling, savory, and surprisingly historical part of many Turkey Day spreads. And there are seemingly as many variations of stuffing as there are households in the U.S., but butter is a unifying and necessary ingredient that no version of this Thanksgiving side can go without. However, if you really want to up the richness and flavor of your next casserole dish of stuffing, forget plain old regular butter and instead try brown butter.

    Industry observers note that brown butter is most notably used in sweet baked goods, but the golden, nutty version can truly enhance pretty much anything where regular butter is used, including savory dishes like stuffing. What it adds to your T-giving side is a sumptuous, caramelly flavor that creates a world of depth and complexity, as the sweetness of the brown butter beautifully complements all the savory ingredients in the stuffing, like the softened bread cubes, sausage (if you use any), and the fresh herbs.

    Don't skimp on it, either. If you're going to use brown butter in stuffing, you'll need to start with quite a bit of butter, perhaps as much as two to three full sticks, because the flavors in your typical stuffing can be bold, and you want to be able to taste the butterscotch-y nuttiness, which pairs so well with sage and onion, or the mushroom in a classic sausage and mushroom stuffing. Even if you make a pumpkin and herb stuffing, full of warming spices and chili, brown butter will enhance the subtle sweetness of the pumpkin and the juiciness of the raisins.

    Industry observers note that if you're inspired to try using brown butter in your stuffing this year for Thanksgiving, but you've never made it before and you're a little intimidated by it, we've a few tips to get you started. First thing, the color of the pan you use matters because you'll want to keep a close eye on how dark the butter is getting — hard to do in cast iron. The choice is yours whether you use salted or unsalted butter, but you'll want to adjust the seasonings in your stuffing accordingly. It's vital that you don't use too high a heat; a good medium to medium-low will do the trick. And finally, don't walk away while your butter is browning because the process is quick, and you can go from delectably golden brown with a nutty aroma to burnt and bitter in a hurry.

    According to recent reports, there are a number of ways to incorporate brown butter into your stuffing, and whichever you choose, you'll want to remove the pan off the heat as soon as the butter is ready. You might add the veggies, aromatics, and herbs directly into the brown butter pan and let those saturate and saute in the nutty goodness, then add them to the bread element. Or you can remove the brown butter from the pan and keep it aside in a bowl, saute the vegetables, add everything into the waiting bowl of butter, and toss to combine.

    #22882. Give Burgers A Protein Boost By Adding One Canned Ingredient To Ground Beef

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (525 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Give Burgers A Protein Boost By Adding One Canned Ingredient To Ground Beef

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When you need protein to help support your body after a workout or to keep you satiated throughout the day, you can reach for a number of foods, but we'd venture that there isn't a tastier option than a hamburger or cheeseburger.
    • Depending on the type of bean you use, a half-cup typically contains between 7 and 9 grams of protein that you can add to your meat mixture, and ultimately, black beans would be our first choice.
    • Recent findings suggest that canned beans are often packed in a gooey liquid that consists of the starches and other substances that seep out of the beans, mixed with water and sometimes a bit of salt.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When you need protein to help support your body after a workout or to keep you satiated throughout the day, you can reach for a number of foods, but we'd venture that there isn't a tastier option than a hamburger or cheeseburger. There are plenty of fast food options that are positively awash in the macronutrient, but cooking at home gives you far more control. Now, ground beef is obviously chock-full of protein, with anywhere from 16 to 24 grams per 4-ounce serving, but if you have a serious goal you need to meet before EOD, there is a canned ingredient that is probably lurking in your pantry (and if it isn't, it should be) that can help push you over the edge. It's beans!

    Depending on the type of bean you use, a half-cup typically contains between 7 and 9 grams of protein that you can add to your meat mixture, and ultimately, black beans would be our first choice. Not only are they closest in color to a perfectly grilled burger, but they're surprisingly meaty. When they're mashed and mixed in with the ground beef, they blend right in, and their mild flavor means they take on whatever seasonings you include without drawing attention to themselves (oh, and there's the added bonus that, in addition to the extra protein, they're also a high-fiber food). By the way, if you don't have black beans on hand, you can absolutely use pinto, cannellini, or even red kidney beans.

    Recent findings suggest that canned beans are often packed in a gooey liquid that consists of the starches and other substances that seep out of the beans, mixed with water and sometimes a bit of salt. As such, they are too wet straight out of the can to use in your burger mixture, so you should drain them and then dry them as much as you can (otherwise, your patties could be a soggy mess). You can even help the process by wicking as much moisture out of them as possible, making for a much more desirable texture, by placing them in a single layer on a baking sheet and popping them in the oven for a few minutes.

    In a recent development, mashing the beans by hand before adding them to the ground beef will always be preferable to the evisceration they'd receive in a food processor. Taking a potato masher (or you could use your meat chopper from the Dollar Tree) to the beans produces a variety of different shapes, which is useful not just for aesthetic purposes (the irregularities in the beans mimic the natural lumps that form when burger patties cook), but also for a more satisfyingly hearty bite.

    Now, beans and ground beef alone do not a burger patty make; you may want to include some binders to help hold everything together. This might be as simple as an egg or two and breadcrumbs — which type of breadcrumbs is totally up to you, because typical fine-textured crumbs will work, as will panko — plus a condiment of your choice, like ketchup, mustard, or even tangy barbecue sauce.

    #22877. For The Best Scrambled Eggs With Extra Fiber, Make Them Turkish Style

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (513 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    For The Best Scrambled Eggs With Extra Fiber, Make Them Turkish Style

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, getting your morning fiber doesn't have to be all about eating more fruits or specialty yogurts.
    • In a recent development, A proper menemen is customizable, but always requires three things: eggs, tomatoes, and peppers.
    • This is without even mentioning the fiber in the peppers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, getting your morning fiber doesn't have to be all about eating more fruits or specialty yogurts. Instead, you can deliciously upgrade your scrambled eggs with classic Turkish vegetables in menemen, a sort of low-effort dish that comes loaded with nutrients.

    In a recent development, A proper menemen is customizable, but always requires three things: eggs, tomatoes, and peppers. It lets you get so much fiber because it starts with sauteing the vegetables until they soften and reduce in size, so you can load up quite a bit in a single meal. While the exact nutritional profile varies between different types of tomatoes, there's an average of about 2.16 grams of fiber per cup. The sauteing step means you can easily add two cups and cook them down to a thick, jammy consistency, providing a delicious brightness to the eggs just over 4 grams of fiber all in one go.

    This is without even mentioning the fiber in the peppers. Banana peppers are relatively high in fiber, clocking in at around 4 grams per cup. Bell peppers are also quite tasty, with some varieties providing about 3 grams per cup. Since the recommended daily fiber intake for most adults hovers between 25 and 38 grams, you could potentially get a substantial portion of your daily needs all in one go. And unlike shakshuka and eggs in purgatory, two similar dishes that traditionally rely on poaching or braising, menemen lets you control the texture quite easily, whether you like your eggs creamy, fluffy, or dense.

    In a recent development, between the rich flavors of menemen and the plethora of foods it can pair with, you've got ample room to deliciously add even more fiber to your breakfast. Taking inspiration from a traditional Turkish breakfast is a great place to start, but don't be afraid to treat your menemen as a starting point rather than a set-in-stone recipe.

    In a recent development, like many countries, Turkey is a major believer in some early morning carbs, and bread products are a great way to add a bit more fiber to your diet. While a slice of white bread may be versatile and provide some sweetness to round out the tomatoes' acidity, one slice also only has about 0.6 grams of fiber. Instead, look to rye, a bread that may not be for everyone but can have three times the fiber of white bread. A slice of pumpernickel can even add 2.7 more grams of fiber to your morning, and the rich, earthy aromas and dense texture are a great contrast to creamy eggs and veggies.

    Few fruits are quite so high in fiber as avocado, with a single medium-sized fruit containing around 10 grams of fiber. As a topping for menemen, its rich creaminess works perfectly with the sharper vegetable flavors, while the eggs provide plenty of protein. Half an avocado smeared over pumpernickel and topped with menemen could provide around 16 grams of fiber from all the different sources, roughly half of what many people need per day.

    #22876. 25 types of meditation and how to choose the right one

    📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3246 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Calm ↗ Open Full Page

    25 types of meditation and how to choose the right one

    📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, clinically reviewed by Dr.
    • Recent findings suggest that the benefits of meditation can reach across your well-being, from reducing stress and anxiety to improving focus and supporting mental and emotional health.
    • We’ve grouped the many types of meditation into six families, so you can see how they relate before you pick one.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, CDCES, MBA.

    Recent findings suggest that the benefits of meditation can reach across your well-being, from reducing stress and anxiety to improving focus and supporting mental and emotional health. But there’s a catch: meditation is a wide family of practices, and the type that works beautifully for your friend might leave you fidgety and frustrated.

    We’ve grouped the many types of meditation into six families, so you can see how they relate before you pick one. Think of it as a menu. Try whichever one draws you in, and let your practice change as you do.

    Meditation is a way to train our attention and awareness so we can be more present in the moment. Most types ask you to rest your focus somewhere, like the breath, a word, a sensation, or a movement, and to notice without judgment when your mind drifts, then return. That returning, over and over, is the practice.

    In a recent development, what changes from one type to the next is where you place your attention and what you hope to cultivate. Some practices sharpen focus, while others cultivate compassion or help the body relax. Many share a thread of mindfulness, noticing where your attention drifts and gently coming back.

    With a history rooted in the spiritual traditions of the East, including Buddhism, Hinduism, and Taoism, meditation has long been recognized as a means to gain enlightenment, self-realization, and balance.

    By exploring the different forms of meditation practice, you can discover what works best for you to enhance your overall well-being.

    Recent findings suggest that these practices share a common aim. You anchor your attention in the present moment and meet whatever arises without judgment. They're a good place to start if you're newly introduced to meditation.

    In a recent development, particularly accessible to beginners, mindfulness meditation invites you to immerse yourself in the present moment. It teaches you to observe your thoughts, feelings, and physical sensations without judgment. By focusing on the breath or the sensations in the body, rather than worries about the past or future, you learn to anchor yourself in the now. This can lead to reduced stress and improved well-being.

    Read more: How to practice mindfulness meditation: 8 tips to get started.

    Recent findings suggest that A body scan moves your attention slowly through the body, one area at a time, noticing sensation without trying to change it. It's a core mindfulness technique and a gentle way into the practice, since you always have your body to come back to. Many people use it to unwind before sleep.

    Read more: Body scan meditation: a step-by-step guide to practice.

    Here the breath is your anchor. You rest your attention on each inhale and exhale, without trying to control the rhythm, and return to it whenever your mind wanders. Because your breath is always with you, this is one of the most portable practices you can carry into a stressful moment.

    Read more: How to practice breath meditation to relieve stress.

    It has been revealed that mindful eating brings full attention to a meal through the senses: the color, smell, texture, and taste of your food, and the signals of hunger and fullness. It can support digestion and help you notice emotional eating patterns with more kindness.

    Read more: How mindful eating can boost your mental and physical health.

    Focus is the whole point here. You rest your attention on one thing, a flame, a sound, or a word, and return to it each time the mind strays. Over time this can sharpen your attention and prepare you for deeper states.

    Sources indicate that concentration meditation is a practice of focused attention, where the mind is directed toward a single point of reference, such as a candle flame, a sound, or the breath. This can help develop focus and attentiveness in everyday life and prepare the mind for deeper states of meditation. This practice can be especially helpful for students, professionals, or anyone looking to improve their cognitive abilities and productivity.

    Read more: Concentration meditation: what is it and how to practice?

    Recent findings suggest that mantra meditation involves the silent repetition of a word or phrase, known as a mantra, to focus the mind and bring deeper states of meditation. This practice can be found in many spiritual traditions worldwide and serves as a powerful tool for calming the mind, reducing stress, and enhancing spiritual growth and a sense of peace and clarity. If you find yourself easily distracted or struggling with a busy mind, mantra meditation can help you maintain focus.

    Read more: Mantra meditation: what it is, benefits, and how to practice.

    Om meditation is a form of mantra practice built around chanting or silently repeating the sound "Om." The vibration of the sound gives the mind something to settle on, and many practitioners find the repetition grounding.

    Industry observers note that read more: What is Om meditation? Plus, a step-by-step guide to practice.

    Also called trataka, candle meditation uses the soft glow of a flame as your focal point. You rest your gaze on the candle, placed at eye level a short distance away, and let it hold your attention. It's a visual anchor for anyone who finds eyes-closed practice restless.

    Read more: Candle meditation: a step-by-step guide to practice at home.

    Industry observers note that visualization meditation guides you to picture a scene, place, or outcome in vivid detail, such as somewhere you feel calm and safe. By giving the mind a rich image to rest on, it can lower stress and support a sense of ease. Unlike open mindfulness, it actively directs the imagination.

    Read more: Visualization meditation: 8 exercises to add to your practice.

    Warmth is the thread running through this family, directed toward yourself, the people you love, and even those you struggle with. These practices can enhance empathy and strengthen your relationships.

    Compassion meditation aims to cultivate feelings of love, kindness, and compassion toward yourself and others. It involves silently directing sentiments of goodwill toward loved ones, acquaintances, and even people we might have a difficult relationship with. It encourages us to see beyond our differences, nurturing a sense of connectedness. A traditional example is Tonglen, a Tibetan practice that pairs the breath with compassion for suffering.

    Read more: Compassion meditation: what it is, benefits, & how to practice.

    It has been revealed that 11. Loving-kindness meditation (metta).

    Loving-kindness, or Metta meditation, is a practice of cultivating an attitude of unconditional love and kindness towards all beings. It starts with developing a loving acceptance of yourself and gradually extends outward to include friends, family, strangers, and even those with whom we may have conflicts. This practice can help break down barriers of anger and division, promoting peace and connection. Though loving-kindness meditation and compassion meditation are closely related and often practiced together, loving-kindness meditation involves sending wishes of happiness, well-being, and peace to yourself and others, whereas compassion meditation specifically focuses on suffering, understanding it, feeling it, and wishing for it to be alleviated.

    Read more: Loving-kindness meditation: what it is, how to practice and why.

    Gratitude meditation guides your attention toward what you appreciate, often by calling to mind a few people or moments you're thankful for. Practiced in the morning or evening, it can lower anxiety and support better sleep, and it pairs naturally with compassion practice.

    Read more: How gratitude meditation can help reduce anxiety.

    Recent findings suggest that sitting still doesn't suit everyone. If stillness makes you restless, these practices let you meditate while the body is in motion, with your attention on each movement.

    Sources indicate that moving meditation brings together deliberate movement and a focused mind. You move with purpose, noticing each step, stretch, or breath as you go. Yoga, tai chi, mindful stretching, and mindful dancing all fall under this heading, and it can be done almost anywhere.

    Read more: The benefits of moving meditation and how to start practicing.

    Recent findings suggest that walking meditation means walking slowly and deliberately, with your attention fully on the act of walking: each step, the movement of your legs, the ground beneath your feet, and your breath. It turns an everyday activity into a practice you can take outdoors.

    Read more: Walking meditation: how to practice and its benefits.

    Mindful movement is the broad practice of bringing present-moment awareness to how your body moves, whether through stretching, yoga, or simple everyday motion. It's mindfulness carried into the body rather than held in stillness.

    Recent findings suggest that read more: What is mindful movement? Plus 9 ways to get started.

    Qigong is a traditional Chinese practice that combines movement, breathwork, and meditation to support balance and focus. In its active form you meditate while flowing through slow, deliberate movements, which makes it a bridge between exercise and stillness.

    Recent findings suggest that read more: What is qigong? Benefits, types, and how to practice.

    Yoga nidra, sometimes called yogic sleep, is a guided rest practice done lying down. A teacher or recording leads you through stages of body scan, breath, and visualization into a state between waking and sleep. No yoga experience is needed, and it's often used for deep rest at bedtime.

    Read more: What is yoga nidra? Plus, why it may be your latest BFF at bedtime.

    A few practices are rooted in a specific lineage and tend to go deeper, often taught within a tradition or by a teacher. Several come from Buddhism, while others, like Transcendental Meditation and kundalini, come from Hindu and Vedic traditions.

    Buddhist meditation is the broad tradition behind many of the best-known techniques, including Zen and Vipassana below, along with loving-kindness. If you want a feel for the tradition as a whole before exploring the specific practices, start here.

    Read more: Buddhist meditation: types, techniques & how to practice.

    Industry observers note that zen meditation, or Zazen, is a disciplined form of meditation central to Zen Buddhism. You sit in a specific posture, focusing on the breath while observing thoughts and sensations as they arise and pass without attachment. Zazen emphasizes the importance of moment-to-moment awareness for a profound sense of peace and insight.

    Read more: Zen meditation: how (and why) to start a Zen practice.

    Vipassana, which means "to see things as they really are," is one of India's most ancient techniques of meditation. It focuses on the deep interconnection between mind and body. Through disciplined attention to physical sensations, you can develop insight into the nature of impermanence, suffering, and egolessness, to move toward enlightenment and liberation. Vipassana meditation is challenging, yet rewarding, offering profound insights into our own minds.

    Read more: Vipassana meditation: what it is, benefits & how to practice.

    Sources indicate that 21. Transcendental Meditation (TM).

    According to recent reports, transcendental Meditation comes from the Hindu and Vedic tradition and was brought to the West in the mid-20th century. It's a silent, mantra-based practice, typically done for about 20 minutes twice a day, and it's taught one-on-one by a certified teacher who gives you your mantra. It's described as effortless, letting the mantra gently carry the mind toward deep rest.

    Read more: Transcendental Meditation versus mindfulness meditation.

    Kundalini meditation is a spiritual practice that aims to awaken what the tradition describes as an inner energy at the base of the spine, using breathwork, posture, and chanting. Practitioners describe effects in spiritual and energetic terms, which are rooted in belief rather than established science. Because the breathwork can be intense, check with your doctor first if you have respiratory, heart, or blood pressure concerns.

    Sources indicate that read more: What is Kundalini meditation? Plus, how to try it yourself.

    In a recent development, chakra meditation focuses attention on the body's energy centers, or chakras, often by visualizing each as a spinning wheel, chanting a sound for each one, or breathing into each area. As with kundalini, the idea of chakras comes from spiritual tradition and is described as belief rather than scientific fact.

    Read more: Chakra meditation: what it is, benefits & how to practice.

    Recent findings suggest that this family works from the body inward. The practices help your nervous system slow down and your muscles release tension, which makes them a good entry point when stress reveals up physically.

    In a recent development, relaxation meditation is an umbrella term for any practice that helps the body release tension and the mind wind down. It often draws on breathing, body awareness, or guided sessions, and it's a gentle place to begin if deeper practices feel like a lot right now.

    A sound bath, where you lie back and listen to instruments, is one example.

    Read more: 5 relaxation meditations that actually work.

    In a recent development, 25. Progressive muscle relaxation.

    Progressive muscle relaxation guides you to tense and then release each muscle group in turn, usually working from the feet up to the face. By targeting the physical side of stress, it can ease tension that anxiety stores in the body, and it pairs well with a body scan to finish.

    Read more: What is progressive muscle relaxation (and how to practice it).

    According to recent reports, the six families above group the 25 types by where your attention goes. This table puts them side by side, so you can compare meditation types and see where to start.

    There’s no one-size-fits-all approach to meditation, and your needs may change over time. The best meditation technique is the one that feels right for you now and fits into your life. These five steps can help you find it.

    Sources indicate that reflect on your goals: Think about what you're hoping to achieve. Whether it's reducing stress, finding inner peace, or developing compassion, your goals can guide your choice of practice.

    Experiment with different practices: Try out different meditation methods and resources, including the Calm app, online courses, and local meditation groups, for guided sessions in different styles.

    Recent findings suggest that listen to your body and mind: Pay attention to how you feel during and after meditation. The right practice should leave you feeling calm and refreshed. If you feel frustrated or strained, try a different type.

    Recent findings suggest that be patient and open-minded: Finding the meditation practice that works for you can take time. Approach each type with curiosity, allowing your experiences to guide your journey.

    Seek guidance: If you're unsure where to start, seek advice from experienced practitioners or meditation teachers for support tailored to your personal journey.

    Starting a meditation practice can bring greater mindfulness and improved emotional well-being. However, establishing a consistent practice can feel daunting. By bringing these tips into your approach, you can build a meditation practice that fits your life and becomes a source of strength and peace.

    Industry observers note that A consistent routine is vital in establishing any new habit, including meditation. Identify a time of day when you can dedicate a few uninterrupted minutes to your practice. For many, morning meditation sets a positive tone for the day ahead. However, if evenings or another time fits your schedule better, make that your meditation moment. Find a quiet, comfortable spot where you can sit or lie down without distractions.

    💙 Morning person? Try this Morning Meditation to set your tone for the rest of the day. Nighttime person? This Deep Rest meditation is for you.

    Begin with just a few minutes each day. Even a short period of meditation can have significant benefits, and starting small makes the practice feel more manageable. As you become more comfortable with the process, you can gradually extend your meditation time.

    💙 Begin your meditation journey with Jeff Warren in this Meditation for Beginners series.

    Meditation is a personal experience, and there’s no single "right" way to do it. Many people form expectations based on others' descriptions, but each person's meditation journey is unique. You don’t need to empty your mind or feel bliss in every session. Notice your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and meet whatever comes up with kindness and curiosity.

    💙 Explore how having Expectations can affect us and our lives with Tamara Levitt on the Daily Calm.

    Recent findings suggest that physical discomfort can be a distraction during meditation. To help settle your body and prepare for stillness, consider some gentle stretching or mindful movement, such as yoga or tai chi, before you begin. This can help release tension in the body and allow you to sit more comfortably.

    💙 Follow along with The Daily Move’s Releasing Stress session to help you unwind before settling down.

    Sources indicate that guided meditations, available through apps, websites, or local classes, can provide verbal instructions and cues to lead you through the meditation process. They can introduce you to different types of meditation, help keep your focus, and offer insights into how to handle common challenges like wandering thoughts or restlessness.

    💙 Try this guided meditation to help you with Reframing Difficult Thoughts whenever your thoughts start to overwhelm you.

    Sources indicate that it’s normal to encounter challenges as you begin your meditation practice. You might miss a day or find your mind wandering constantly. When this happens, treat yourself with kindness and compassion. Each time you notice your mind has drifted and come back to the present moment, you’re practicing.

    💙 Practice this Loving Kindness meditation to guide you in cultivating feelings of kindness toward yourself and others.

    Join a meditation group or find a community of practitioners that can provide support and a sense of connection. Sharing experiences with others on a similar path can be incredibly encouraging.

    There’s no single agreed list, but these three approaches are often used to sort the many types of meditation:.

    Recent findings suggest that concentration meditation: You rest your attention on a single point of reference, such as the breath, a mantra, a sound, or a candle flame. When your mind wanders, you return to it.

    Mindfulness meditation: You widen your awareness to include thoughts, sensations, and your surroundings as they arise. It is often taught as part of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

    Loving-kindness meditation (Metta): You build goodwill and warmth toward others, starting with yourself.

    Industry observers note that the idea of levels in meditation can vary depending on the tradition or practice. A way to think of meditation depth might include the different types and states.

    Physical relaxation: The initial stage where the body relaxes deeply.

    Concentration: The mind begins to focus, reducing distractions.

    Mindful awareness: A state of heightened awareness of the present moment.

    Deepening peace: Inner silence becomes more profound.

    Insight: Understanding about yourself and reality may arise.

    Blissful states: Experiences of joy or profound contentment.

    Transcendence: A sense of unity or oneness with all, often considered the deepest level of meditation.

    The power of a meditation practice can vary from person to person, depending on individual needs, preferences, and goals. Some may find mindfulness meditation helpful for managing stress and enhancing self-awareness, while others prefer the structured approach of Transcendental Meditation or the heart-opening practices of loving-kindness meditation.

    Ultimately, the most ‘powerful’ type is the one you’ll keep practicing. Try a few to see which fits.

    How I Get Free Traffic from ChatGPT in 2025 (AIO vs SEO)
