    #22869. Industry News: Olive Garden's Buttery Breadstick Topping Is Actually Dairy-Free

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (527 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Olive Garden's Buttery Breadstick Topping Is Actually Dairy-Free

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that many diners would agree that one of the biggest pleasures of dining out at Olive Garden isn't just the ambiance or even the appetizers or entrees, like the Tour of Italy, but rather one of the complimentary items that comes with your meal: breadsticks.
    • Margarine differs from butter in that it is made from oils with a variety of additional ingredients, including water.
    • Industry observers note that butter can also resolidify after it cools, potentially giving the breadsticks a pasty coating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that many diners would agree that one of the biggest pleasures of dining out at Olive Garden isn't just the ambiance or even the appetizers or entrees, like the Tour of Italy, but rather one of the complimentary items that comes with your meal: breadsticks. These soft, pillowy sticks of dough are buttery, garlicky, and great for dipping into dressing or sauces. They are so popular that the chain of Italian-inspired restaurants goes through a staggering number each week, and many diners may even request some extra when taking home leftovers. But despite the buttery flavor of this signature item, it doesn't actually contain any real butter. Instead, the firm uses margarine.

    Margarine differs from butter in that it is made from oils with a variety of additional ingredients, including water. Together, they form an emulsion that can resemble butter. While not all brands of margarine are completely dairy-free, the kind Olive Garden uses doesn't contain any dairy at all, making it suitable for diners with dairy allergies or those who abstain from animal-derived foods. One reason Olive Garden may use margarine instead of butter is that it can provide a smoother, more consistent topping for its breadsticks.

    Industry observers note that butter can also resolidify after it cools, potentially giving the breadsticks a pasty coating. According to Reddit users, Olive Garden uses liquid margarine, which retains its consistency. Additionally, margarine is generally less expensive than butter, and in an industry with razor-thin margins, anywhere you can save money can lead to greater profits.

    Recent findings suggest that perhaps the best use of margarine for Olive Garden fans is to recreate a homemade version of its iconic breadsticks. You can start by using Great Value Garlic Bread Sticks — a fantastic store-bought dupe, available at Walmart — and brushing melted margarine over the sticks after they're heated for an extra buttery finish. Or you can use the melted margarine to give latest life to any of the chain's leftover breadsticks you bring home.

    According to recent reports, margarine's uses extend well beyond breadsticks, though. For starters, many types of margarine retain a soft texture even when refrigerated, meaning you can easily spread it onto bread or toast even when it's cold. Try doing that with regular butter! Because some types of margarine contain little to no milk solids, they also don't burn as easily as traditional butter does. This means that you can use them to pan-fry foods at relatively higher temperatures than you can with butter without as much risk of altering the flavor of the finished dish.

    Finally, margarine is also great for baking. You can often use it in place of butter in the same quantities, though the substitution may affect the finished product. Certain types of margarine also remain solid at higher temperatures, which can be beneficial when baking things like pastries, where fat that melts too quickly can make the difference between beautiful, puffy layers and a flat, greasy end result. Just be sure to avoid spreads or squeezable margarine for baking, as the water content can be too high and negatively affect your recipe.

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (536 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Not Bacon: Give Grilled Cheese A Southern Twist With This Hearty Ingredient

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that giving your grilled cheese a Southern twist doesn't mean you have to start using buttermilk biscuits and lard.
    • The same thing that makes ham hocks delicious also makes them a bit difficult to use.
    • Ham hocks are especially good when you "reuse" them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that giving your grilled cheese a Southern twist doesn't mean you have to start using buttermilk biscuits and lard. Instead, you can use ham hocks, a seasoning meat that isn't always actually eaten but is always enjoyable.

    The same thing that makes ham hocks delicious also makes them a bit difficult to use. Loaded with bone, connective tissue, and extremely tough meat, bringing out their flavor potential requires a lot of low-and-slow cooking. You may have more luck using smoked ham hocks for a deeper cure and smoke profile, though both smoked and raw hocks still require a long simmer to fully break down the tough collagen before transferring the meat to a sandwich. Regardless, adding shredded ham hock to grilled cheese gives you a tender, protein- and fat-laden ingredient that practically melts right alongside your gooey cheese.

    Ham hocks are especially good when you "reuse" them. Cooking one dish with ham hocks and then using the meat in another lets you easily transfer complex flavors, a major tip for making any grilled cheese better. Hocks cooked in Southern-style collard greens adopt a perfectly moist texture and pick up acidity from vinegar and vegetable notes from the greens and onions. Similarly, ones cooked with black-eyed peas have a next-level creaminess, adopting earthy aromas to round out your sandwich. Still, if you want to preserve the smokiness of a fresh smoked ham hock, you can always simmer it for a couple of hours until the meat and skin fall apart, giving you a budget-friendly alternative to pulled pork.

    It has been revealed that using ham hocks in your grilled cheese opens up latest opportunities, since they're laden with fat and can make excellent use of leaner cheese varieties. Still, you should also consider what part of the hock to use, as some parts have more flavor than others and may require different ratios.

    Typically, grilled cheese sandwiches rely on fatty, moisture-rich cheeses because they melt better than drier, aged varieties and carry that rich flavor profile. While you'll still want to use enough for a good texture, ham hocks provide plenty of decadence in their own right, so you can add a heavier sprinkle of Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano, aged Gouda, or Manchego viejo. These underrated cheeses can cut through heavier fats more easily and are immediately noticeable even in small quantities, giving you a chance to add more complexity.

    Recent findings suggest that when you work with a smoked ham hock, you'll quickly notice how intense the skin's flavor is. Rich in fat and smoky flavor, this is a versatile ingredient you can mash into a spread for your bread, provided it's been properly simmered, or slice thinly and sprinkle in with shredded cheese. The meat directly under the skin is usually pinker and less potent, so it's a great choice if you're looking for more protein but not quite as much smoke. Meat from the top and bottom of the hock may offer a good middle ground, potentially holding more richness and smoke than interior meat but not quite as much as the skin, though this can vary depending on how the hock was smoked and prepared.

    #22860. Upgrade Your Next Omelet With One Sweet Pantry Staple

    📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (510 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Upgrade Your Next Omelet With One Sweet Pantry Staple

    📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Omelets are one of those dishes that feel made to be upgraded.
    • A sweet omelet may sound a bit strange, but it's more common than you might think.
    • According to recent reports, for your first honey omelet, you may want to use something light, like honey made from orange blossom or clover nectar.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Omelets are one of those dishes that feel made to be upgraded. While meats and vegetables go a long way toward something savory, going in a sweeter direction mixes things up and makes great use of one ingredient you probably already have on hand: honey.

    A sweet omelet may sound a bit strange, but it's more common than you might think. Jelly omelets were a hit 100 years ago, and many Japanese folks love atsuyaki tamago, a rolled type of omelet that can be made with sweetened dashi stock. Using honey instead achieves a similar effect but gives you far more control over how your dish turns out. A drizzle over the top while it's still hot warms the honey, helping it spread more evenly and ensuring every bite is as sweet as you want it. Still, you can always mix a dash directly into the eggs, distributing the honey's sweetness throughout the omelet and potentially encouraging a bit of browning as it cooks.

    According to recent reports, for your first honey omelet, you may want to use something light, like honey made from orange blossom or clover nectar. These aren't overly intense and carry floral notes, and the addition of these aromas can make anyone's mouth water. If you're working with particularly rich eggs, especially duck eggs, you may want to use something with a bit more body, like wildflower or sunflower honey. These have the necessary depth of flavor to stand up to other ingredients and are great when you want a strong honey taste but not too much sweetness.

    Industry observers note that honey can be a pretty potent ingredient, so adding too much extra sweetness with reduced tomatoes or caramelized onions can make your dish a bit too decadent in the morning. Instead, try going in the opposite direction, finding ways to add different kinds of saltiness, spice, and astringency for a complex blend of deliciousness.

    According to recent reports, A swicy flavor profile combines heat from capsaicin and sweetness from honey, both of which balance each other out and go great with eggs. Pork and honey also go together like peas and carrots, so a dollop of chorizo or spiced deli meats in an omelet brings umami, complexity, and harmonious flavors. This is a great opportunity to use hot honey as well, giving you more flexibility with other additions while still getting the same end result. Plus, spicy ingredients can add great color, improving the presentation of your dish to really wow your breakfast guests.

    According to recent reports, the best cheeses to add are usually sharp, salty, and earthy. Aged parmesan, extra-sharp cheddar, and really anything laden with salt crystals and pungency help balance the sweetness without overshadowing your honey's delicate flavors. Similarly, a bit of raw green onion can taste truly magnificent with honey and egg, but there's an emphasis on "a bit." Too much means you can't taste the honey, so try to aim for a miserly pinch at first and dial in your preference on subsequent attempts.

    #22858. REA: The Open-Source AI Tool That Can Reverse Engineer Almost Anything (2026 Guide)

    📅 05 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2854 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Blogspot ↗ Open Full Page

    REA: The Open-Source AI Tool That Can Reverse Engineer Almost Anything (2026 Guide)

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blogspot

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • What if you could ask your AI assistant how any app works and get a real answer, backed by evidence, without ever seeing the source code?
    • What if you could ask your AI assistant how any app works and get a real answer, backed by evidence, without ever seeing the source code?
    • You use an app, tap a feature, and wonder how it was built.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What if you could ask your AI assistant how any app works and get a real answer, backed by evidence, without ever seeing the source code? You use an app, tap a feature, and wonder how it was built. Maybe it is a fast search bar, a clever clipboard trick, or a mechanic in an old game. Until recently, finding out meant months of learning disassemblers and reading assembly code. A new open-source project called REA changes that. It has earned more than 430,000 stars on GitHub, and in this guide I will explain what it does, which problems it solves, and how you can start using it today. In this guide The problem with reverse engineering How REA solves it How REA works What REA can analyze Real examples How to get started REA at a glance Using REA responsibly Frequently asked questions The Problem: Reverse Engineering Is Hard Reverse engineering is the practice of studying finished software to understand how it works. It is powerful, but it has never been beginner-friendly. If you have tried it, or even thought about trying it, you have probably run into these obstacles. 1. A steep learning curve Reading assembly code and pseudocode takes a long time to learn. Many curious developers give up before they get their first useful result. 2. Too many tools and no single workflow An Electron app needs one approach. An Android APK needs another. A .NET assembly, a native binary, and a website each have their own tools, file formats, and tricks. 3. Slow, manual investigation Even experts can spend hours following one function through strings, calls, and references just to understand a single small feature. 4. AI answers you cannot verify If you ask a general chatbot how an app works, it may give a confident answer that is simply invented. Without evidence, you cannot tell what is real. 5. Painful setup Connecting analysis tools to an AI agent usually requires custom scripts and configuration, and it is easy to break. The Solution: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) REA is a free, MIT-licensed project that connects your AI agent to professional reverse engineering tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol). MCP is a standard way for AI agents to use external tools. In simple terms, REA acts as a bridge between your agent and the software you want to understand. Here is how it answers each problem above. The Problem How REA Solves It Steep learning curve You ask in plain English. Your agent runs the tools and explains the results. Too many tools One MCP server covers native binaries, Electron apps, Android, .NET, websites, and dozens of other formats. Slow and manual The agent traces code, references, and calls for you. Answers you cannot verify Every result includes the evidence and limitations behind it. Painful setup One command registers REA with your agent and backs up your existing configuration. You do not need the app’s source code. You point your agent at the app, ask a question, and REA helps it trace the answer. How REA Works You ask a question. For example, how a feature in a particular app works. The agent calls REA. It uses MCP to inspect the target and trace the relevant code. REA returns findings. These include code, references, and clearly marked unknowns. The agent acts on them. It can explain the behavior, ask follow-up questions, or write and test its own version of the feature. The same workflows are available from the terminal, so you can also script them without an agent. Analysis runs locally on your machine. Your agent receives the tool results, and your AI provider’s own data policy applies to that part. What Can REA Analyze? The range of supported targets is one of REA’s biggest strengths. These are the main groups. Native programs and binaries REA returns pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references. Deep native analysis uses an engine you already have, such as Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, or Kuna. It also supports GNU objdump and Rizin for offline inspection. JavaScript and Electron apps This is the easiest place to start, because static JavaScript analysis needs no native engine. REA recovers modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC connections, and native add-on relationships. Android apps and devices REA can inspect APK manifests, classes, decompiled methods, signatures, and resources. Through adb, it can also look at packages, processes, and logs on an emulator or a real phone. Flutter apps and JEB projects are supported too. .NET and managed code For .NET assemblies, REA reads metadata, CIL instructions, and native dependencies without running the program. Websites and network captures REA can inspect page structure, scripts, and network activity using a Chrome-family browser. It can also read saved HAR and Fiddler SAZ files to examine requests, responses, and exposed payloads. Specialist formats The list continues with Go and Rust binaries, GPU code objects, GGUF and safetensors model files, Unity IL2CPP metadata, Godot PCK archives, PE imports and certificates, ELF notes, Linux kernel modules, WebAssembly, EVM bytecode, SQLite databases, firmware images, packet captures, and PyInstaller executables. Most of these use built-in static inspection, so no extra software is required. Real Examples: What Has REA Done? The project publishes several case studies on its website. DX-Ball sound panning. REA followed a sound call into a helper function and turned incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passed 3,205 test cases against the original x86 code and matched all 63 compiled function bytes. Notion’s clipboard bridge. REA traced how Notion’s Electron app moves clipboard data from the renderer through preload and IPC into the main process, including the rich clipboard format. TH04 bullet patterns. REA recovered the angle calculations of a classic DOS game and compared the rebuilt C++ with the original compiler output. Bonus: build RL environments from a web app REA can record a web app session and turn its API calls into tools an AI agent can use. It then exports a runnable environment for reinforcement learning or for testing how well an agent completes tasks. With a saved HAR file, the command looks like this: rea environment-build ./session.har ./my-env --name my-env --json You then run the result with AgentEnv and Docker, and add your own tasks and reward checks. How to Get Started With REA You need Node.js and npm. The project lists supported Node versions as 22.x (22.23.4 or newer), 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), or 26.12.1 and above. Step 1: Run the setup command npx rea-agents setup Step 2: Choose your agents and approve the changes Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents. It shows you the proposed changes first and keeps backups of your existing configuration. Step 3: Restart your agent The new MCP server is loaded when the agent starts again. Step 4: Ask your first question Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. Prefer the terminal? You can inspect an extracted Electron app or ASAR file directly: npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json To keep REA installed, run npm install --global rea-agents. REA changes rapidly, so use rea enhancement to stay current. Updating is also the first fix to try if you run into a bug. REA at a Glance What makes it special REA combines the reach of dozens of analysis tools with the convenience of an AI agent. It helps you understand software you do not have source code for, and it backs each conclusion with evidence instead of guesses. The range of supported formats, from native binaries to Electron apps to Android devices, is unusually broad for a free tool. Key features Works through MCP with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents Evidence and limitations attached to every result Local analysis on your own machine A full command-line interface for scripting Support for dozens of file and app types An RL environment builder Guides and case studies on the official website Pricing REA itself: free and open source (MIT license) Commercial engines such as IDA Pro, Hopper, and JEB: you must obtain these legally under their own licenses Ghidra: a free option for native analysis; see the setup guide for details Perfect for Developers, security researchers, students, software preservationists, and anyone who wants to understand how an app works. Using REA Responsibly Use REA only on software you own or are authorized to examine. The project is intended for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you have permission to study. It does not permit cracked tools, stolen license keys, or bypassing license restrictions. Read the project’s disclaimer before you start. Also be careful where you download it from. The project warns that a similar repository name or a copied README does not make a download official. Use only these sources: GitHub: github.com/morluto/rea Website: rea.tools npm package: rea-agents Frequently Asked Questions Do I need Hopper or Ghidra? Only for deep native binary analysis. JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native engine, and setup can install Hopper with your approval. Does REA upload my app? No. Analysis runs locally. Your agent sees the results, and its provider has its own data policy. Which AI agents work with REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers can use it. What should I do if I find a bug? Update first, because a recent release may already include the fix. If the problem continues, open an issue on GitHub with your REA version, the target type, the steps to reproduce, and the error output. Final Thoughts The old problem was simple: understanding software without source code took too much skill, too many tools, and too much time. REA’s answer is just as simple. It gives your AI agent the tools to investigate, and it requires the agent to show its evidence. Whether you want to learn how a favorite feature works, study a classic game, or inspect an Electron app, REA is a strong place to start. Just make sure you use it only on software you are allowed to examine.

    What if you could ask your AI assistant how any app works and get a real answer, backed by evidence, without ever seeing the source code?

    You use an app, tap a feature, and wonder how it was built. Maybe it is a fast search bar, a clever clipboard trick, or a mechanic in an old game. Until recently, finding out meant months of learning disassemblers and reading assembly code. A new open-source project called REA changes that. It has earned more than 430,000 stars on GitHub, and in this guide I will explain what it does, which problems it solves, and how you can start using it today.

    In this guide.

    It has been revealed that reverse engineering is the practice of studying finished software to understand how it works. It is powerful, but it has never been beginner-friendly. If you have tried it, or even thought about trying it, you have probably run into these obstacles.

    Reading assembly code and pseudocode takes a long time to learn. Many curious developers give up before they get their first useful result.

    Industry observers note that an Electron app needs one approach. An Android APK needs another. A .NET assembly, a native binary, and a website each have their own tools, file formats, and tricks.

    Even experts can spend hours following one function through strings, calls, and references just to understand a single small feature.

    If you ask a general chatbot how an app works, it may give a confident answer that is simply invented. Without evidence, you cannot tell what is real.

    Connecting analysis tools to an AI agent usually requires custom scripts and configuration, and it is easy to break.

    REA is a free, MIT-licensed project that connects your AI agent to professional reverse engineering tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol). MCP is a standard way for AI agents to use external tools. In simple terms, REA acts as a bridge between your agent and the software you want to understand. Here is how it answers each problem above.

    Sources indicate that you do not need the app’s source code. You point your agent at the app, ask a question, and REA helps it trace the answer.

    The range of supported targets is one of REA’s biggest strengths. These are the main groups.

    In a recent development, REA returns pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references. Deep native analysis uses an engine you already have, such as Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, or Kuna. It also supports GNU objdump and Rizin for offline inspection.

    This is the easiest place to start, because static JavaScript analysis needs no native engine. REA recovers modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC connections, and native add-on relationships.

    REA can inspect APK manifests, classes, decompiled methods, signatures, and resources. Through adb, it can also look at packages, processes, and logs on an emulator or a real phone. Flutter apps and JEB projects are supported too.

    For .NET assemblies, REA reads metadata, CIL instructions, and native dependencies without running the program.

    It has been revealed that REA can inspect page structure, scripts, and network activity using a Chrome-family browser. It can also read saved HAR and Fiddler SAZ files to examine requests, responses, and exposed payloads.

    Recent findings suggest that the list continues with Go and Rust binaries, GPU code objects, GGUF and safetensors model files, Unity IL2CPP metadata, Godot PCK archives, PE imports and certificates, ELF notes, Linux kernel modules, WebAssembly, EVM bytecode, SQLite databases, firmware images, packet captures, and PyInstaller executables.     #22857. Breaking: What is EMDR therapy, and does it actually work?

    Breaking: What is EMDR therapy, and does it actually work?

    📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Maybe a friend swears EMDR helped her move past something she’d carried for years.
    • Industry observers note that if you’re uncertain, that’s understandable, because EMDR can sound unconventional: you briefly recall a painful memory while following side-to-side stimulation, like tracking a moving target with your eyes.
    • Here’s what EMDR involves, what the research reveals, and what a session is like, so you have a clearer picture of whether it might make sense for you.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

    Maybe a friend swears EMDR helped her move past something she’d carried for years. Or maybe you came across it online while searching for ways to cope with a memory that still feels heavy. Whether you’ve heard of EMDR but don’t know how it works, or you’re familiar with the approach but skeptical, we’re here to break it all down.

    Industry observers note that if you’re uncertain, that’s understandable, because EMDR can sound unconventional: you briefly recall a painful memory while following side-to-side stimulation, like tracking a moving target with your eyes. But the research tells a more reassuring story. It’s a well-studied therapy for trauma, and it’s increasingly explored for anxiety and depression, too.

    Here’s what EMDR involves, what the research reveals, and what a session is like, so you have a clearer picture of whether it might make sense for you.

    EMDR stands for eye movement desensitization and reprocessing. It’s a structured therapy that helps the brain reprocess distressing memories so they carry less emotional weight. Psychologist Francine Shapiro, PhD, developed it in the late 1980s after she noticed that certain eye movements seemed to ease her own troubling thoughts.

    It has been revealed that EMDR rests on Shapiro’s adaptive information processing model. The idea is that your brain normally files an experience away, so you can recall it later without feeling like you’re living it again. But a frightening or painful event can interrupt that process, leaving the memory raw and unfiled, still carrying the fear and detail of that moment. That’s why it can resurface later, as vivid as the day it happened.

    According to this model, “processing” a memory means helping your brain finish the filing. You don’t forget what happened, and the facts don’t change. What changes is the emotional charge it carries, so recalling it feels less like reliving it and more like remembering it. To help that happen, EMDR uses a technique called “bilateral stimulation.”.

    EMDR uses a technique called bilateral stimulation. While you hold a difficult memory in mind, a trained therapist guides you through side-to-side stimulation.

    Bilateral stimulation can take a few forms:.

    eye movements that follow your therapist’s fingers.

    gentle taps that switch between your hands or knees.

    tones that play in one ear, then the other.

    There’s a theory behind the side-to-side part, though researchers are still working out exactly why it helps. The leading explanation is about mental bandwidth. Your working memory, the part of your mind that holds what you’re focused on right now, can only handle so much at once. When you track side-to-side movement while recalling a hard memory, the two tasks compete for that limited space. The hard memory tends to feel a little less vivid, and with repetition it can lose its sharp edges, so it feels less overwhelming to hold.

    💙 Learn more in our guide to bilateral stimulation.

    EMDR has eight phases, though they tend to blend together in practice. The early phases cover your history and teach you coping skills, so you feel prepared before any hard memories arise. In the middle phases, you focus on a specific memory while following bilateral stimulation, which is meant to help your brain reprocess it. The final phases check that the memory feels less distressing and help you close out the work safely.

    The evidence is strong for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a condition that can develop after a frightening or life-threatening event. A Cochrane review (a gold-standard summary of research on a topic) found that EMDR and trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) both reduce PTSD symptoms. They also outperformed other therapies when researchers checked in after treatment ended. A 2024 review in the Journal of Traumatic Stress identified more than 30 randomized controlled trials supporting EMDR for PTSD in adults and children. Major health organizations, including the World Health Organization, recommend EMDR for PTSD.

    Sources indicate that however, some guidelines, including those from the American Psychological Association (APA), rate the evidence for EMDR as less certain than for trauma-focused CBT. Researchers also debate exactly why EMDR works.

    💙 Read more about how EMDR can help you cope with PTSD.

    The picture is more mixed outside PTSD. Early research suggests EMDR may help with anxiety, as one meta-analysis found reduced symptoms of anxiety, panic, and phobia, though the studies were small and varied in quality.

    Evidence for depression is emerging as well. Another meta-analysis highlighted reduced depression symptoms, with the strongest effects in more severe cases. These findings are promising, but they don’t carry the same weight as the PTSD research.

    After you and a therapist finish the early phases, you bring a specific memory to mind and notice the thoughts and body sensations that come with it. Then your therapist guides you through the bilateral stimulation while you let your mind go where it goes. You can ask to pause or stop at any time. Unlike many talk therapies, EMDR doesn’t require you to describe the memory in detail.

    Sessions usually run 60–90 minutes. Your therapist pauses often to check in on what you noticed. Over several rounds of bilateral stimulation, many people find the memory feels less sharp, even though the facts don’t change. Between sessions, a mindfulness practice, such as slow breathing or a body scan, can help you ease feelings that surface.

    💙 Explore Calm's EMDR-Inspired Bilateral: Anxiety, a set of music tracks that alternate gently between your left and right ear. It draws on the bilateral stimulation used in EMDR, though audio-only versions haven’t been studied on their own the way clinical EMDR has. Think of it as a calming complement to therapy, not a replacement for a trained therapist.

    Sources indicate that the answer varies, since it depends on what you’re working through. For a single, recent trauma, some people notice their symptoms ease within a handful of sessions. More complex or long-standing trauma usually takes longer, sometimes many months. Therapists describe a typical course as 6–12 sessions, though it varies widely from person to person.

    Industry observers note that along the way, some people feel worse before they feel better. Painful memories can stir up strong emotions in the short term, which is common and doesn’t mean EMDR isn’t working. Before reprocessing begins, your therapist teaches you coping skills, such as grounding exercises that anchor you in the present, so you have tools to use if those feelings get intense.

    Industry observers note that 💙 Try the 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 practice, a quick way to ground yourself in the present, with Prof. Megan Reitz.

    Industry observers note that EMDR stands for eye movement desensitization and reprocessing. It’s a form of therapy that uses bilateral stimulation, such as guided eye movements, to help your brain process distressing memories so they feel less intense. Psychologist Francine Shapiro developed this therapy in the late 1980s.

    In a recent development, EMDR may help with anxiety, though PTSD is where the evidence is strongest. The studies on anxiety are smaller and less consistent. If your anxiety is tied to a specific frightening experience, it may be worth asking a therapist whether EMDR fits your situation.

    💙 Explore how mindfulness can help you manage your anxiety.

    Sources indicate that EMDR differs from talk therapy because it doesn’t require you to describe your experience in detail. You’ll still talk with your therapist, especially early on, but the reprocessing happens while you hold a memory in mind and follow bilateral stimulation. Talk therapies like cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) focus more on examining and reshaping your thoughts out loud.

    The main benefit of EMDR is that it can ease the distress tied to painful memories. For many people with PTSD, that can mean fewer flashbacks and less of that constant, on-alert feeling.

    Much of the debate is about why EMDR works, not whether it does. The evidence is strongest for PTSD, with early and more mixed findings for anxiety and depression.

    In a recent development, some studies suggest the eye movements themselves add little. The benefit may instead come from giving your mind a second task while you recall a memory, which can make it feel less vivid and emotionally intense. Other tasks that split your attention may have the same effect.

    Recent findings suggest that certain guidelines, including the APA’s, consider the evidence for EMDR less established than for trauma-focused CBT. None of this takes away from the relief many people find with EMDR. It’s useful context as you weigh your options with a therapist.

    EMDR is generally safe when a trained therapist delivers it, though you may experience some short-term effects. You might feel more emotional or tired between sessions, or have vivid dreams as your brain keeps processing the memory.

    Industry observers note that these reactions usually pass within a day or two. If they last longer or feel overwhelming, it’s a good idea to tell your therapist, who can adjust the pace with you. Serious side effects are uncommon when a therapist follows the full eight-phase process.

    It has been revealed that the number of sessions you need depends on the memory you’re addressing and how long it has affected you. Some people feel relief after a few sessions, while longer-standing experiences often take more time. A common range is 6–12 sessions, but your timeline may be shorter or longer. Your therapist can give you a better sense of what to expect once they know your history.

    According to recent reports, full EMDR needs a trained therapist, so it’s not something to try on your own. A therapist helps you reprocess memories and stay grounded if one feels overwhelming, which matters most with intense trauma.

    💙 Mindfulness practices and Calm’s EMDR-Inspired Bilateral: Nervous System Reset program can help you feel calmer at home.

    According to recent reports, mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

    Industry observers note that pair everything with Aldi's Rosemary Artisan Crackers ($3.49) (bonus points if you have some real rosemary to use as decor).     Recent findings suggest that okay, so this may not technically qualify as a charcuterie board, but that term tends to be very forgiving these days.     Aldi's Roasted Garlic & Tomato Basil Monterey Jack Cheese ($3.49) and Onion & Chive Double Gloucester Cheese ($4.19) are a great duo to anchor this board, and a Spinach Artichoke Dip ($2.99) adds even more flavor and creaminess. Along with Aldi's Garden Vegetable Crackers ($1.79), you can serve up all of your herby, cheesy goodness with some fresh crudités using Gourmet Mixed Baby Carrots ($2.99) (which happen to be adorable) and a pound of radishes ($1.45) for added crisp and color.     According to recent reports, instead of your typical bread or crackers, you can build this board around Aldi's mini bagels ($3.85), which will be the perfect vehicle for soft, herby cheeses like everybody's favorite Boursin Garlic & Fine Herb Cheese ($6.05) and a Chive & Onion Cream Cheese Spread ($1.99).     Sources indicate that some like it hot, and those people can find plenty of options at Aldi to set their mouths on fire. Make things (painfully) fun with a spiced-up charcuterie board featuring some of Aldi's hot and spicy products.

    Now for the dips, include the Hot Honey Dip ($2.79) for a bit of sweet heat, and the Piquillo Pepper & Artichoke Bruschetta ($3.09) for another delicious element that offers a bit more sweetness than spice to balance things out. Finish it all off with Aldi's Sea Salt & Pepper Scalloped Crackers ($1.99) for dipping and dunking.

    Pickled and pickle-flavored foods seem to be all the rage lately, so why not lean in? Turn your party into a pickle party by building a fully pickled-out charcuterie board at Aldi for that punchy hit of briny, vinegary goodness.

    In a recent development, two types of cheese will be at the center of the pickle party: the Dill Havarti Cheese ($2.75) (a creamy Danish-style cheese) will keep you on theme while the Extra Sharp Latest York Cheddar Cheese Cubes ($3.29) will cut all that vinegar with salty sharpness.     From there, you obviously need some actual pickles. Go for Great Gherkins Kosher Baby Whole Dill Pickles ($2.09), which are the perfect size for snacking. Stick to Aldi's Original Crisp Crackers ($1.79) to accompany everything so your cracker doesn't compete with all of the flavors you've already got going on.

    In a recent development, lastly, for all those out there with a sweet tooth, there are lots of ways to incorporate notes of sweetness into your "charcuterie" board while still keeping it fairly savory (this one foregoes the meat as well).     The Cocoa Cardona Cheese ($4.95) at Aldi is a goat's milk cheese with a cocoa powder rind, giving you just a hint of chocolate, and the Honey I'd Rather Bee at the Sea Sea Salt Honey Cheddar Cheese ($3.85) also offers a delicate balance of sweet and salty. And the Chocolate Chip Cannoli Dip ($3.29), decidedly more sweet than savory, is a cream cheese-base dip that'll go perfectly with Benton's Belgian Butter Waffle Crisps ($2.19).

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A bowl of chili welcomes a wide array of renditions.
    • Sources indicate that using the Mediterranean herb in the Tex-Mex recipe may sound unusual, but the flavors align surprisingly well.
    • Garten's rendition works the basil into a tomato sauce base, full of sweet bell peppers and onions, lightly recalling a pasta sauce in composition.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A bowl of chili welcomes a wide array of renditions. You can make the dish red or green, use proteins like turkey, pork, or chicken instead of the classic beef, and include many aromatics in the mix. Each detail makes a chili rendition unique. Even a fresh herb gives a bowl a whole new character — just look toward Ina Garten's inclusion of basil. Ina Garten often uses basil as a swap for cilantro, so her inclusion of the herb in her chili makes sense.

    Sources indicate that using the Mediterranean herb in the Tex-Mex recipe may sound unusual, but the flavors align surprisingly well. Garten uses basil's mildly citrusy sweet and lightly peppery flavor specifically in a chicken-based chili, integrating the herb during both the initial simmering stage and as a final garnish. It's a one-two combo that establishes an herbal character that infuses into every bite, lending more than just a basil-inflected finish.

    Garten's rendition works the basil into a tomato sauce base, full of sweet bell peppers and onions, lightly recalling a pasta sauce in composition. Still, seasonings like cumin, chili powder, and a dash of spicy cayenne appear in the mix, cementing the dish as a bowl of chili, only brighter and more herbal in nature.

    It has been revealed that ina Garten's tips for cooking chicken perfectly dependably deliver, but don't rule out employing the basil in chili recipes with other proteins, too. The herb also works well in an extra-hearty bean and brisket rendition that's spiced with chiles and even coffee. Cooked down right alongside the kidney beans, basil lends the legumes its distinct herbal character, all without becoming a cornerstone flavor. You can try out such a technique in a classic ground beef chili, too; using the herb early in cooking makes it one of many layered flavors.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're after a more basil-forward spin, consider working the herb into a ground turkey chili recipe. You can still go heavy on the spice, using chili powder and jalapeños alongside garlic powder and cumin. Add dried basil early on and raw basil atop the finished chili, and you'll get a delicate bowl, herbal-tasting and fresh, yet still pretty classic.

    Sources indicate that and for a more inventive approach, take a page from Thai cuisine, specifically Phat ka-phrao (stir-fried basil beef). Made with sturdier Thai basil, this version of the herb stands up better to heat. Saute the meat alongside extra-spicy chiles, lots of garlic, and this type of basil, and you can lay down the foundation for an extra-bold chili, still delicious over rice or with tortilla chips.

    #22850. Can you be friends with your ex? What to consider first

    📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1440 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Calm ↗ Open Full Page

    Can you be friends with your ex? What to consider first

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that your phone buzzes.
    • Sources indicate that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing.
    • Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that your phone buzzes. It’s your ex, sending a meme you would’ve laughed at together six months ago. You smile, then wonder why you smiled.

    Sources indicate that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing. For some people, staying connected feels natural because the habit, and maybe the care, is still there. For others, it makes healing feel harder. Every situation is different, and you’re allowed to take your time figuring out what works for you.

    Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.

    In some cases, you may be able to. Post-breakup friendships can be healthy and meaningful when the breakup was mutual, the relationship had little conflict, and both people have had time to grieve.

    That remarked, every friendship between exes is different. Researchers who study friendships after breakups describe two kinds. In one, both people have moved on and value the connection. In the other, one or both people stay in touch because of lingering attraction or reluctance to end things. The first kind can be rewarding. The second can make it harder to get over the breakup.

    Sources indicate that the dynamic you had with your ex matters, too. A study found that relationships shaped by high conflict, emotional dependency, or attachment anxiety may be harder to turn into a friendship afterward.

    Before you decide anything, it may help to reflect on why you want to stay in touch. A few questions to sit with:.

    What am I hoping this friendship gives me?

    Am I trying to stay close to them or avoid the discomfort of letting go?

    How would I feel if they started dating someone new?

    If the last question stings, it may just mean that you need more time.

    If you were the one who ended things, you might want friendship out of guilt or a wish to soften the loss. If you were the one who was left, you might view friendship as a potential path to getting back together.

    If the answers don’t come right away, try a mindfulness practice. A few minutes of reflection or a short breathing exercise can help you sort through what you’re thinking and feeling.

    💙 Try the Pause to Check In meditation on the Calm app.

    It has been revealed that if you’ve thought it through and still want to stay in touch, a few signs suggest a friendship may work. People who are securely attached often find it easier to stay friends after a breakup, but the list below can apply to anyone:.

    You both see the breakup as mutual, with no ongoing hurt, resentment, or blame.

    You’ve both accepted that the romantic relationship is over, with no unresolved romantic feelings.

    There’s a reason for the friendship beyond comfort or familiarity, such as shared values, kids together, or a work connection.

    In certain cases, staying friends can make healing harder or keep you from pouring energy into fresh parts of your life:.

    You’re still in love with your ex and hoping the friendship leads somewhere.

    The relationship involved emotional manipulation, control, or abuse.

    The friendship gets in the way of new relationships, like when a new partner feels uneasy about your connection.

    You have different expectations for the friendship, which could leave one of you hurt.

    💙 Discover the signs of having a toxic ex.

    It can be, especially since staying in touch can make it harder to let go. One study found that regular contact with an ex may slow emotional recovery. When you’re still part of each other’s routines, it can be harder to mourn the end of the relationship.

    By contrast, a low-contact friendship, where you talk occasionally and keep to limits you’ve agreed on, is less likely to hold either of you back.

    How you feel after you talk is worth paying attention to. If you often feel sad, anxious, or unsettled, or you keep replaying the conversation, it may help to take some space.

    💙 Read more on how to deal with a breakup when you’re hurting.

    In a recent development, it may be appropriate to be friends with your ex, depending on your situation. It tends to work best when you’ve both moved on, the breakup didn’t involve harm, and the friendship fits both of your lives. If it also feels honest and comfortable to you, that’s a good sign.

    According to recent reports, being friends with an ex isn’t automatically a red flag. If your partner is friends with an ex, how they handle it matters more than the friendship itself. A few questions to consider:.

    Transparency: Do they talk about it openly, or does it feel secretive?

    Priorities: Do they make time for you and the relationship?

    Boundaries: Are there clear limits on the friendship, or does contact feel constant and undefined?

    Responsiveness: When you raise a concern, does your partner listen or dismiss it?

    If something doesn’t sit right, you could bring it up and see whether they listen, get defensive, or brush you off. If you’re the one staying friends with an ex, your newly introduced partner’s concerns are worth hearing out, even if nothing is wrong.

    You don’t have to keep in touch with your ex after a breakup. Taking space is often healthy and necessary, and you can change your mind later. You can choose a full break, a time-limited break (“let’s not talk for a few months”), or a low-contact friendship.

    Sources indicate that if you do stay in touch, some boundaries may protect your well-being. A few to consider:.

    Sources indicate that set a pace. Daily texting can pull you back into old routines, so try starting with occasional check-ins instead.

    It has been revealed that decide what’s off limits. That might mean dating lives, old conflicts, and late-night “remember when” talks.

    It has been revealed that give yourself space online. Mute or unfollow for a while to adjust without ending the connection.

    Blueprint a review and a way out. After a few months, ask whether the friendship still feels good. If it doesn’t, have a line ready, like “I think I need to take a step back for now.”.

    It has been revealed that if you share children, a workplace, or a friend group, you may need to stay in touch. It’s often best to stick to logistics, like pickup times for the kids or project deadlines at work.

    💙 Explore the Boundaries meditation on Calm.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s no set amount of time to wait before trying to be friends with an ex. Some people feel ready within months, while others take years. Some never feel ready or choose not to be friends, and that’s okay.

    A question to ask yourself is whether you can feel okay about the thought of your ex moving on. If that still hurts, you probably need more time.

    Yes, being friends with an ex can sometimes turn into getting back together. Whether that’s a good thing depends on why your relationship ended and whether those reasons have changed.

    Sources indicate that problems tied to circumstances, like bad timing or distance, may be easier to work through than core differences, like values, long-term goals, or how you communicate. If you get back together and those core differences haven’t changed, the same patterns can resurface.

    It’s painful when one of you wants to stay friends after a breakup and the other doesn’t, and what helps depends on which side you’re on.

    If you’re the one being asked, you’re allowed to say “not yet” or “no.” If you’re unsure, you don’t have to answer right away. You might say:.

    “I care about you, and I need some time before I know what this looks like.”.

    “Can we revisit this in a few months?”.

    “I’m not able to be friends right now, and I hope you can respect that.”.

    Industry observers note that if you’re the one who wants friendship, the kindest move is to respect the space your ex has asked for. If you push for contact, it can get harder for you both to move on, even if giving them room hurts.

    💙 Check out our guide on how to cope with rejection.

    Mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

    Sources indicate that tuna salad is a pragmatic yet delicious dish, easily crafted using pantry staples. Open up some canned fish packed in oil or water, mix with store-bought mayo, then fold in some aromatics, and you'll have yourself a tasty classic. It's a tried-and-true formula that welcomes many other shelf-stable components, like panko bread crumbs, for example. You only need about 2 tablespoons per can of tuna to round things out nicely.

    Recent findings suggest that the delicate breadcrumb style is wonderfully versatile in the kitchen, and its texture enhances tuna salad, too. The foodstuff lends the dish more body, without turning it too dense. The panko absorbs moisture, making the crumbs turn soft while still retaining airiness, in turn creating an extra-tender salad. The panko also thickens the dish, giving your meal more structure. Not to mention, a bite here or there might still remain crunchy, upping the textural intrigue.

    Recent findings suggest that it's an advantageous set of qualities unique specifically to panko; you won't want to reach for a different breadcrumb in this application, as they may be too dense. This Japanese foodstuff is made using a unique electric cooking process, producing a delicate crumble without any bread crust. Other breadcrumb varieties are simply too heavy for the task. So grab a package of panko online or in stores to make a tuna salad rendition with a textural twist.

    Not sure how to round out a tuna salad with panko? The options are wide-ranging. You could keep to a straightforward mix of tuna, mayo, salt, and pepper — perfect for a tuna sandwich filling — or go with the many potential tuna salad upgrades. Walnuts or kimchi, for example, add body and even more texture to the dish.

    It has been revealed that similarly, to complement panko's delicate composition, throw in some vegetables. Green onion, celery, and an herb, say parsley, dill, or cilantro, are tried-and-true tuna salad enhancements. And don't overlook a tangy fermented bite, whether in the form of pickles or pickled onions for a truly amped up tuna salad. You could also imbue brightness using vinegar or even lime juice, which will aromatically soak into the panko.

    Sources indicate that alternatively, consider playing to the breadcrumb's East Asian origins, using other Japanese ingredients in the dish. You could add a couple spoonfuls of miso into the dressing for complex savory flavors, as well as sesame seeds and oil for a discernible nutty touch. Or go down the spicy tuna route, incorporating a hot sauce like Sriracha into the build — especially tasty when wrapped in seaweed. Swap the standard mayo for a Japanese-style emulsion, mix in the panko, and you'll have yourself a magical tuna salad foundation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    According to recent reports, when many of us think "hot breakfast," we tend to naturally gravitate toward thoughts of scrambled eggs. Aside from the fact that, when prepared correctly, they are tender, delicate, and fluffy (or custardy, depending on how you like them), eggs are considered the gold standard for protein, so they are quite wholesome as well. On their own, though, they can get a little monotonous, especially if you're making them every day, so it does help to add an ingredient here or there. And if you happen to enjoy omega-3-rich cold-smoked salmon, well, it pairs seamlessly with a classic scramble, boosting both the flavor and the protein content.

    Industry observers note that once considered an expensive delicacy, smoked salmon is quite popular now in the U.S., and as a result, it's much easier to find at your local grocery store (even Aldi carries its own version, and it can be found at Walmart, too). Cold-smoked salmon, despite the fact that it tends to be packed in super-thin slices, is buttery and velvety. While it does taste fishy, there are also light, smoky notes that give it a deeply savory flavor, which works beautifully when combined with the mild egg scramble. Additionally, a serving (which will vary in size) might contain anywhere from 12 to 18 grams of protein, which is great if you have daily goals you want to meet or you're just looking to get more of the macronutrient in general.

    Truly, the most difficult part about incorporating smoked salmon into your scramble is cooking the eggs to the right consistency without burning or browning them. All you have to do with the salmon is slice the ultra-thin pieces into slivers or small squares. Once your eggs have reached the texture you desire, you'll take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon. That's literally it; you don't have to actually cook the salmon over direct heat because it's so delicate that the residual warmth of the scrambled eggs will gently bring it up to temperature.

    It has been revealed that now, because smoked salmon is so light and thin, you might want your eggs to match that energy, so create a fluffy, soft texture with a bit of cream whisked in. Alternatively, you could take a page out of Bobby Flay's book and fold in a dollop of crème fraîche, or really up the decadence and melt in some cubes of cream cheese (and take care not to overcook anything, because smoked salmon with burnt, rubbery eggs? No thanks). Also, because all of the elements involved are either rich or thick, a sprinkling of something green, like fresh chives or dill, or even a little parsley or tarragon, would brighten things up, both aesthetically and in terms of flavor.

    #22839. Tech Report: Forget Expensive Ribeye: A Cheaper Cut For Delicious Beef Stroganoff

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (545 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Forget Expensive Ribeye: A Cheaper Cut For Delicious Beef Stroganoff

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good.
    • While it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak.
    • Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good. But one thing that might not lift your spirits is the price. Classic stroganoff starts off with strips of thinly sliced beef, with cuts like ribeye being among the best picks. We're not here to fault ribeye, which has earned its price for a reason, but if you want to knock a few dollars off your next batch, try swapping in ground beef instead.

    While it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak. The texture is bound to be different, and you'll need to adjust how you cook it, but good-quality ground beef still has the rich, beefy flavor that pairs so well with the tang of sour cream, earthy mushrooms, and the sweet depth of cooked-down onions, all at a significantly lower cost.

    Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time. Traditional beef stroganoff relies on expensive cuts that are prized for their tenderness and quick-cooking nature. Cheaper, tougher cuts like chuck or round usually need hours of braising to soften, which doesn't suit a dish that's meant to come together promptly. Ground beef, however, is often made from those same economical cuts, and the grinding process does all the tenderizing mechanically. That means you're getting all that mouthwatering flavor without the waiting, guaranteeing a tasty, Boomer-approved meal.

    According to recent reports, if you make the switch from ribeye to ground beef, you'll want to do a few things differently. First, check out the numbers on your ground beef packaging. You're looking for a blend that doesn't shy away from fat, something like an 80-to-20 lean-to-fat ratio, or even 70-to-30. Like ribeye, these fattier blends are packed with rich flavor, and the fat that'll render out will elevate the sauce, just in a different format. Go any leaner and you risk dry, chewy beef pebbles floating in your sauce.

    With ribeye, standard practice is to slice the beef ultra-thin, give it a quick sear, then let it simmer in the sauce for a few minutes. The process for ground beef is similar, albeit with a few caveats. For starters, there's no slicing, so you're already saving time. Like ribeye, you want to get the meat nicely browned. Our personal advice is to add the beef to the pan in small handfuls and flatten each one with the back of a spoon, which allows it to brown without overcrowding the pan.

    It has been revealed that remove the beef from the pan once it's seared, which isn't usually done with ribeye. Even in a fattier blend, ground beef has far more exposed surface area than your average slice of steak, so it risks drying out if it's left to simmer for too long. For the most tender results, build your sauce first, then add the beef back in and stir once you're just about ready to serve. Don't worry about the flavors not melding, since the fat and fond left behind from searing will be doing most of the heavy lifting.

    • You might not expect it, but sandwich chains are holding it down when it comes to Italian subs.
    • "They do it right," one Reddit user said, referencing the Original Italian.
    • It's worth noting that an old-school-style Italian sub owes it all to the Italian immigrants who populated this country throughout the 19th and 20th centuries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You might not expect it, but sandwich chains are holding it down when it comes to Italian subs. Of course, there is no denying the appeal of a small, locally owned shop, but there are many reasons why you might opt instead to head into a chain to get your Italian hoagie fix, the most obvious of which is proximity. But there is also the fact that some chains just make darn good food. Food Republic did its research and compiled a list of the best chain Italian subs based on customer reviews, and each entry brings its own unique flavor to the table. But only one, the No. 13 Original Italian from Jersey Mike's, can claim to be the best old-school version of this particular sub.

    "They do it right," one Reddit user said, referencing the Original Italian. They continued by stating that if they had a classic Italian deli near them, they'd go there, but since they don't, "it's Jersey Mike's without question." Another user in that same thread agreed, writing, "I love this sub and am always a little amazed [it comes from] a chain" and not, presumably, from a traditional deli. And over on Google, a reviewer shared that the Original Italian reminded them of a sub they'd had during their childhood and expressed their gratitude that "there is a place that can make a real Italian hero like the old days.".

    It's worth noting that an old-school-style Italian sub owes it all to the Italian immigrants who populated this country throughout the 19th and 20th centuries. There are a few stories about how the hoagie came to be, including one based in Philadelphia (where it's the official sandwich of the city) involving shipyard workers and their distinctive lunches. There is another version that describes how Giovanna Amato sold filling sandwiches to dockworkers in Maine. Whatever its origins, the classic Italian sub came to be characterized by Italian meats and cheeses, a variety of fresh, crisp vegetables, a savory dressing, and an oily, vinegary drizzle.

    Recent findings suggest that jersey Mike's Original Italian proves a chain can still honor those old-school roots. It checks every box, from five different Italian meats to provolone cheese to the default setting, Mike's Way, which includes onions, lettuce sliced super-thin, and tomatoes, as well as red wine vinegar and an olive oil blend, plus two impactful seasonings: salt and oregano.

    It has been revealed that but of course, Jersey Mike's serves 21st-century customers who like having options, so the sandwich, in addition to scratching an old-school itch, can also serve as a jumping-off point for some. You might, for example, upgrade your Original Italian sub by choosing the rosemary parmesan bread instead of plain white. There are a number of additional toppings available as well, such as jalapeño peppers, dill pickles, and hot chopped pepper relish.

    #22833. Skip Gruyère: This Norwegian Cheese Boasts Nutty Flavor & Fewer Calories

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (592 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Skip Gruyère: This Norwegian Cheese Boasts Nutty Flavor & Fewer Calories

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cheese is one of life's greatest pleasures, but no two varieties are quite the same.
    • Jarlsberg is instantly recognizable thanks to its large, round holes, and while traditional Swiss Gruyère might lack these holes, it matches Jarlsberg's intensely nutty flavor — although how the two cheeses develop their respective flavors is very different.
    • Despite sharing a similar taste, their nutritional profiles tell a different story.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cheese is one of life's greatest pleasures, but no two varieties are quite the same. Knowing your way around your mozzarella and parmesan is a useful skill that won't just impress your dinner guests but will also transform the way you use cheese in the kitchen. Take Gruyère, for example. If, say, a French onion soup recipe calls for it, and you've had no luck finding it at the store, any cheese connoisseur will tell you that Norwegian Jarlsberg makes an excellent substitute. The two share a similar nutty flavor and melt beautifully, with Jarlsberg also serving a lower-calorie option.

    Jarlsberg is instantly recognizable thanks to its large, round holes, and while traditional Swiss Gruyère might lack these holes, it matches Jarlsberg's intensely nutty flavor — although how the two cheeses develop their respective flavors is very different. Jarlsberg gets it from a proprietary bacterial culture called Propionibacterium shermanii, a sub-sect of Propionibacterium freudenreichii. During fermentation, this culture consumes lactic acid to produce propionic acid and carbon dioxide. The acid contributes to the cheese's nutty profile, while the carbon dioxide becomes trapped in the cheese, creating those large holes. Gruyère takes a different approach, developing its signature flavor through a combination of factors, including the unique composition of the high-altitude Alpine milk, its bacterial cultures, and a longer aging process.

    Despite sharing a similar taste, their nutritional profiles tell a different story. Jarlsberg contains around 100 calories per ounce, compared with up to 120 calories for Gruyère. That's a modest saving of 20 calories per ounce, which can swiftly add up if you're using a generous amount in a grilled cheese or fondue. So if you're looking for a slightly lighter alternative to Gruyère without sacrificing flavor, Jarlsberg makes for a wonderful swap.

    Recent findings suggest that as is the case with Gruyère, one of Jarlsberg's biggest selling points is its versatility. You can always enjoy it as is, pairing it with grapes, crackers, and cold cuts as part of an elegantly presented charcuterie board, or keep things simple and serve it alongside a glass of wine; Jarlsberg goes particularly well with chardonnay and sweet rieslings, as well as low-tannin reds like pinot noir. While there are plenty of ways to enjoy the cheese without cooking it, we think the best way to get the most out of Jarlsberg is to take advantage of its meltability.

    Sources indicate that jarlsberg's flavor is comparatively milder than that of sharper Gruyère, making it an excellent substitute if you're after a nutty, creamy cheese that won't overpower everything else, which makes it a great contender for a grilled cheese. If you still want some of Gruyère's intensity, simply combine the two. Their complementary flavor profiles mean neither cheese should overpower the other, giving you a nutty filling with plenty of depth. In a nod to Jarlsberg's Norwegian roots, add in some fresh dill, pickles, and a generous helping of cold-smoked salmon for a Scandi-inspired twist.

    In a recent development, another great way to put Jarlsberg to work is as a pizza topping. Its mild, buttery flavor and excellent meltability make it an obvious fit. Rather than tomato sauce, pair it with mushrooms, caramelized onions, and fresh thyme to let the cheese shine. If white pizza isn't your thing, swap the dough for Danish rye bread to create your own smørbrød, a charming Scandinavian open-faced sandwich. Simply take the buttered bread and add your toppings of choice, layer the Jarlsberg on top, then blast it in the broiler until creamy and gooey.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tuna salad typically already comes with plenty of protein and flavor, but boosting these virtues can give you something even more delicious and nutritionally dense. This is especially true if you use boiled eggs, an easy-to-prepare ingredient that's highly compatible with whatever recipe you prefer.

    Exact needs vary based on body type and medical history, but most adults need a minimum of about 0.36 grams of protein per pound of body weight daily. Beginning a recipe with canned tuna, which hovers around 22 grams of protein per 3-ounce serving, is a good start, but it can be better. A single boiled egg contains roughly 6 grams of protein and is rich in umami, no matter what texture you cook it to. The whites add a lovely, soft chew to counteract the density of fish meat, while the yolks themselves sort of disappear into the mayonnaise to boost its richness.

    It has been revealed that if you use the best mayo for tuna salad — Kewpie, which is packed with MSG — you'll get an extra umami bomb. Between the fish, egg, and MSG, you have all the makings of a hearty, satisfying meal, whether you eat it straight or heat it up in a melt. The end result is something that tastes more decadent than it does nutritious, full of velvety textures and rich flavors that make it seem like you spent quite a bit of time perfecting your recipe. Combine it all with minced veggies and pickles, and you get something comprehensively nourishing that's ready in a flash.

    It has been revealed that eggs can be so much more than simply hard-boiled, so you've got plenty of options when it comes to the exact tastes and textures you want your tuna salad to have. Some bulk out a bowl, some focus on the sauce, and still others can add delightful upcoming textures, but all are quite easy.

    According to recent reports, if you want something with an unobtrusive texture but a great amount of flavor, then boil your eggs for a jammy yolk. The runnier center diffuses through the mayonnaise, infusing it with flavor before it coats every piece of fish. If you're looking for something different, you can pan-fry hard-boiled eggs to crisp up the exteriors and add a touch of roasted flavor to a comparatively fresh and cool dish. If you use a flavored oil, like chili oil or one infused with herbs, this is an easy way to add upcoming seasonings to the overall dish.

    Eggs can either introduce a dichotomy of textures or disappear into the meal, depending on your preference. Leaving your eggs whole or cut in half lets you spoon them into individual bites, preventing your meal from being too one-note. On the other hand, finely dicing them into crumbles is the best way to get their flavor into every nook, cranny, and ingredient. Using an egg slicer can give you the best of both worlds, creating thin slivers of white while the yolk dissolves into the mayonnaise.
